title: Manager II, Technical Enablement Management
location: Seoul, South Korea; Sydney, Australia; Tokyo, Japan
description:
We are Datadog's in-house product experts. The Technical Enablement Management (TEM) team empowers customers through technical training sessions, ensuring they maximize the value of Datadog. We combine deep technical knowledge with a consultative approach, demonstrating best practices and tailoring training to specific use cases.

As a Manager on this team, you will play a critical role in strengthening our relationships with Sales and Customer Success teams across APJ, developing and coaching the Technical Enablement Managers (TEMs) who report to you, and evolving our enablement programs to better support customer adoption and success. You will lead a distributed team of Technical Enablement Managers covering markets across Asia and ANZ. Manager 2 leaders at Datadog are people-first managers, trusted collaborators, and operational owners. In APJ you will also be the most senior enablement voice in the region, so you will spend as much time building awareness and credibility with Sales and Customer Success as you do managing delivery.

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

What You'll Do:

  • Own the positioning and enablement strategy for Sales and Customer Success teams in APJ, driving attach rates by positioning training as a value-added service and increasing consumption of complimentary offerings
  • Build demand upstream: engage Sales and Customer Success teams across the region at scale, keep positioning and materials current, and drive consistent use of the request process
  • Act as the quality gate for incoming work, scoping requests to the right offering, focusing broad asks into targeted sessions, and aligning demand to business need
  • Analyze customer training adoption and feedback, evaluating programs for ROI to inform which offerings to scale, evolve, or retire
  • Develop sales tools and enablement resources that help internal teams confidently position and sell training to customers
  • Drive consistency in training delivery, content utilization and reporting across the team, evaluating delivery quality and distinguishing facilitation gaps from content gaps
  • Build and maintain the intake and capacity-planning mechanisms the team runs on, including pre-session questionnaires, triage, prioritisation frameworks and accurate time tracking, and continuously iterate on tooling and processes to improve efficiency and scalability
  • Lead, coach and mentor a team of TEMs across APJ, conducting regular 1:1s, performance evaluations and session shadowing, identifying performance gaps early and managing performance formally when coaching alone is not enough
  • Proactively monitor team KPIs (utilization, CSAT, productivity, session delivery against demand, and attendance rates), diagnosing trends and gaps, and assign workload so that TEMs achieve an 80% productivity target while balancing training delivery, content creation and enablement activities
  • Champion the use of AI tools within the team to improve productivity from content creation and session prep through to reporting and QA, coach TEMs on effective and responsible use, and identify opportunities to apply AI to scale enablement delivery and improve program ROI
  • Actively participate in recruiting, hiring and onboarding across the team and the broader organization
  • Collaborate with Technical Solutions leadership, Sales, Customer Success, Engineering and Product teams to address urgent needs and implement process improvements

Who You Are:

  • An experienced people manager, results-driven, with a strong focus on executing strategies that drive measurable business impact and revenue growth
  • A strong coach and mentor who invests in career development and builds inclusive, high-performing teams, and who has authored the things that let a team scale: career progression frameworks, structured onboarding and a consistent coaching cadence
  • Has built demand for a services or enablement function by going out to Sales and Customer Success rather than waiting for inbound requests, and can point to a measurable before and after
  • A clear communicator who can influence without authority and align stakeholders around common goals
  • Energised by bringing a service to new internal audiences, and able to make the case as compellingly on the twentieth telling as on the first
  • Able to hold priorities firmly when demands compete, renegotiating scope with partner teams while keeping the relationship strong
  • Deliberate about priorities, with a track record of choosing what not to take on and delegating rather than absorbing
  • Culturally adaptable across Japan, Korea, Southeast Asia and ANZ, adjusting approach per market rather than applying one style everywhere
  • Direct and transparent, setting clear expectations and healthy boundaries, and calm when plans change at short notice
  • Exceptionally self-organised, owning their own scheduling, follow-up and administrative rhythm
  • A strategic thinker who balances customer needs with business goals, evaluates program ROI and drives cross-functional alignment, with a track record of implementing scalable enablement programs in a growing company
  • Data-driven, comfortable using metrics and KPIs to inform decisions and optimize performance
  • Demonstrated capability of utilizing AI tooling and scaling it, with a growth mindset of embracing change and being curious
  • Technically proficient, with knowledge of modern infrastructure, monitoring solutions, and cloud technologies
  • Experienced (5+ years) in Training, Presales, Post-Sales, Consulting, or another customer-facing role, with a history of success
  • Educated in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent experience
  • Requires up to 25% travel across the APJ region, primarily to drive and promote enablement adoption with Sales and Customer Success along with team development and cross-functional planning

description:

description:

The SDS group’s mission is to be the world’s easiest-to-use tool to discover, classify, manage, and report sensitive data risks across cloud, on-premise, and code environments. title: Manager I, Engineering - Husky
description:
Husky is what we call the distributed, petabyte-scale columnar event store at the heart of our Event Platform, which powers dozens of Datadog’s most popular products – Logs, RUM, APM, Cloud Network Monitoring, Netflow, and many more. Husky was built from the ground up at Datadog to store and query massive volumes of event data at low cost, with data fully queryable within seconds of arrival.

As an Engineering Manager on Husky, you will lead one of a few closely collaborating teams that work directly on Husky’s internals. We own the full lifecycle of events stored by our Event Platform – whether it’s managing the ingestion of over 100 million events per second exactly-once, optimizing the persistence layer with lightning-fast compaction, tweaking our columnar format, timely deletion across hundreds of thousands of customer tables, or building the metadata service that enables hundreds of thousands of queries per second – you will be responsible for the growth and success of a team constantly meeting new scalability requirements driven by Datadog’s growing customer base and suite of products.  

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships that it builds, the creativity it brings to the table, and the collaboration of being together. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our employees can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

 

What You’ll Do: 

  • Manage a team of software engineers ranging from new grads to senior engineers, focusing on career development, inclusivity, and high impact

  • Be a technical leader of the team; while the role may not involve frequent hands on coding, you’ll be reviewing architecture decisions, RFCs, and pull requests and ensuring what the team ships is high quality

  • Partner with product teams to evaluate use cases, ensure smooth implementation, and prioritize new platform capabilities. 

  • Share on-call responsibilities with the rest of the team and ensure a culture of operational excellence

  • Scale a petabyte-scale database to an exabyte-scale one

 

Who You Are:

title: Manager I, Engineering - Cloud FinOps
description:
Datadog's Cloud FinOps team answers a question the business runs on: what does each product and each customer actually cost us to serve? Finance uses this team's output to close Datadog's books, Product uses it to compare cost to serve against what a customer pays, and engineering leaders use it to catch cost movements before they compound. As the Engineering Manager for this team, you'll own delivery across the runtime pipeline, coverage onboarding, and cost-to-customer identity mapping. You'll own the contracts that Finance and platform teams depend on. The core engineering problem is reproducibility: every dollar of cloud cost is placed against the product and customer that caused it, with lineage on every result and closed periods that replay exactly. This role starts by closing a coverage gap and grows into owning the model every platform team at Datadog onboards through.

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships that it builds, the creativity it brings to the table, and the collaboration of being together. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our employees can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

What You'll Do:

  • Lead and grow a team of engineers building the platform that allocates Datadog's cloud cost to products and customers, setting the operating rhythm across runtime and release, coverage onboarding, and identity and mapping.
  • Own the publication contract with Finance: versioned metrics with effective dates, backfill, and reproducible history, so any closed period can be replayed on demand and trusted for close.
  • Own the metric contracts with platform teams across Engineering, shifting cost facts to the teams that generate the cost so coverage growth stops scaling linearly with your headcount.
  • Partner with Revenue Engineering on the cost-to-revenue identity join that turns cost data into margin per product and per customer.
  • Drive continuous improvement in product and customer cost coverage and accuracy, and hold delivery commitments with teams that don't report to you.
  • Reduce key-person risk on runtime and compiler architecture by spreading ownership across the team, and use AI tooling (Claude Code, Cursor, and similar) to raise the team's speed and leverage.

Who You Are:

  • An engineering leader with experience managing data platform or data engineering teams building batch and pipeline systems judged on correctness and reproducibility.
  • You've shipped versioned publication with effective dates, backfill, and reproducible history.
  • You've held a delivery commitment with a team outside your reporting line, and you can describe what happened the first time a contract was missed.
  • You bring domain experience in metering, usage-based billing, cloud cost, revenue data, or financial data platforms.
  • You operate without a product manager in the loop on the external half of the job: you set the contracts, negotiate the boundaries, and drive the roadmap yourself.
  • If you've owned systems whose output is audited or closed by Finance (SOX scope, month-end close, revenue recognition), graph datasets or built retrieval-grounded systems where every answer cites its source and you know where a model shouldn't be trusted with a number at all, that is helpful experience.

Datadog values people from all walks of life. We understand not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That's okay. If you're passionate about technology and want to grow your skills, we encourage you to apply.

title: Manager, Field Enablement EMEA
location: Amsterdam, The Netherlands; Dublin, Ireland; London, United Kingdom
description:
The Team

Our GTM Enablement team plays a critical role in helping Datadog's Sales, SDR, and Customer Success teams succeed by equipping them with the right skills, knowledge, and tools at the right time. We partner closely with teams across Sales, Customer Success, Product Marketing, Curriculum, and Operations to ensure enablement programs translate into real performance in the field.

If you like adding value and seeing the direct impact of your work through the people you lead, and you thrive in dynamic environments where you can roll up your sleeves and get things done, this role is for you.

The Opportunity

Datadog is investing further in EMEA, and we're looking for a Manager, Field Enablement to lead our team of Field Enablement Managers supporting Sales, SDR, and Customer Success across the region — a frontline people leadership role where you'll manage, coach, and grow your team while helping execute the enablement strategy and quality bar for EMEA.

You'll partner closely with EMEA Sales, SDR, and Customer Success leadership, as well as Enablement Curriculum, Program Management, and Operations teams, to translate regional priorities into a coordinated enablement plan across markets and segments — keeping your team's programs tightly aligned with our global Field Enablement standards.

This role is ideal for someone who has excelled in field/sales enablement and leadership, cares as much about developing enablement practitioners as developing sellers and CSMs, and wants to help build the enablement leadership layer for one of Datadog's fastest-growing regions.

What You'll Do

  • Spearhead the Field Sales Enablement team’s transition from facilitators/trainers to data-driven business partners and coaches who are able to proactively identify GTM knowledge/performance gaps and deliver targeted enablement solutions that drive behavior change
  • Manage, coach, and develop your team of Field Enablement Managers — regular 1:1s, goal-setting, performance feedback, and career growth plans calibrated against the Field Enablement career path.
  • Own workforce planning for the EMEA team, including recruiting, interviewing, and onboarding new Field Enablement Managers as headcount and market coverage scale.
  • Set the enablement strategy and priorities for EMEA in partnership with Sales, SDR, and Customer Success leadership, translating regional business goals into a coordinated plan across your team.
  • Establish and maintain a consistent quality bar for delivery — facilitation standards, coaching rigor, program effectiveness, and AI fluency — through practice sessions, calibration exercises, and delivery reviews.
  • Serve as the strategic partner and escalation point for EMEA Sales, SDR, and CS leaders, coaching your team to turn field listening into insight that shapes enablement priorities and regional recommendations.
  • Keep EMEA aligned with the global Field Enablement organization: partner with the Director and other regional leaders on standards and certifications, represent EMEA in global forums, and report team impact and outcomes to stakeholders.

Who You Are

  • 7+ years of experience in sales enablement, field enablement, training, or a related GTM role, including direct experience as a Field Enablement Manager or equivalent senior individual contributor.
  • Prior experience managing people directly, or clear, demonstrated readiness to step into people management — including experience hiring, onboarding, and scaling a team, ideally in a fast-growing or newly-formed function.
  • Deep understanding of the EMEA GTM landscape, with experience supporting Sales, SDR, and/or Customer Success teams across multiple markets and languages.
  • Track record of partnering with senior Sales, SDR, and CS leadership to translate business priorities into enablement strategy, backed by excellent stakeholder management, communication, and influence skills.
  • Strong coaching orientation — certified coach (e.g., ICF ACC/PCC, Co-Active CTI, or equivalent) preferred, or a demonstrated commitment to developing one — paired with expert facilitation experience and familiarity with sales methodologies (MEDDICC, Command of the Message, Challenger, Sandler, etc.).
  • Data-driven approach to enablement — comfortable using sales performance data, field feedback, and qualitative insights to set priorities and measure impact; experience with Asana or similar project management tools is a plus.
  • Fluent in English (additional European languages a strong plus), and willing and able to travel approximately 30% across EMEA.

Why This Role Matters

As the first people leader for Datadog's EMEA Field Enablement team, you'll build the leadership layer that helps a growing team of Field Enablement Managers do their best work — and, in turn, help Sales, SDR, and Customer Success teams across EMEA ramp faster, sell better, and retain more customers. You'll shape how enablement scales as a function in one of Datadog's most complex and fastest-growing regions, with a direct line to the Director of Field Sales & CS Enablement.

title: Manager, Accounts Payable
description:
About the Role

We are seeking a Manager, Accounts Payable to lead Accounts Payable and Expense operations. This role will manage individual contributors and may oversee team leads while ensuring invoices, payments, reconciliations, tax reporting, and employee expenses are processed accurately and on time.

The Manager, Accounts Payable will own team performance and execution while driving process improvements, automation, and reporting. You will work across Procurement, Accounting, Treasury, Tax, Finance, and other teams to resolve complex issues, strengthen controls, and improve the procure-to-pay experience.

The ideal candidate is a reliable people leader who uses business context and data to make decisions, advises stakeholders, and delivers measurable operational improvements.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead, coach, and develop AP and Expense team members.
  • Manage team performance, staffing, workload allocation, and day-to-day execution.
  • Build a high-performing team with clear expectations, strong accountability, and consistent results.
  • Oversee invoice processing, purchase order matching, coding, approvals, payments, vendor inquiries, and employee expense operations.
  • Ensure AP and Expense activities are completed accurately, on time, and in accordance with company policies and controls.
  • Own balance sheet reconciliations, AP close activities, accrual support, aging reviews, and related reporting.
  • Lead annual 1099 reporting and support other AP-related tax and compliance requirements.
  • Serve as the primary AP contact for internal and external audits, ensuring requested documentation is accurate and complete.
  • Monitor unmatched invoices, open purchase orders, payment exceptions, duplicate payments, credits, and other outstanding items.
  • Identify inefficiencies across AP and Expenses and lead process improvements that increase accuracy, efficiency, and scalability;
  • Drive automation and AI initiatives related to invoice processing, matching, approvals, reconciliations, exception handling, and reporting.
  • Develop reporting and insights using tools such as Zip, Ramp, Tableau, ERP systems, and other operational data sources.
  • Establish and monitor performance metrics, including processing volume, aging, cycle times, exception rates, and on-time payments.
  • Partner across Procurement, Accounting, Treasury, Tax, Finance, and business teams and lead cross-functional initiatives when needed.
  • Evaluate complex issues using business context, advise team members and stakeholders, and recommend practical solutions.
  • Escalate risks and issues that could affect costs, controls, service levels, or short-term business goals.

What You’ll Bring

  • 7+ years of experience in accounts payable, Expenses, accounting operations, or procure-to-pay, including people-management experience.
  • Proven ability to lead teams, manage performance, and deliver reliable results.
  • Experience owning and improving an operational area with measurable impact.
  • Strong knowledge of invoice processing, purchase orders, payments, expense management, reconciliations, accruals, and the monthly close.
  • Experience managing 1099 reporting and supporting internal and external audits.
  • Experience using procurement or finance platforms such as Zip, NetSuite, and Ramp.
  • Sound judgment when addressing diverse challenges, applying policies, and escalating financial or operational risks.
  • Strong cross-functional collaboration, communication, and stakeholder-management skills.
  • Demonstrated ownership, accountability, and reliability in a high-volume environment.
  • A bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

description:
Datadog is seeking an experienced Legal Operations Manager to join our Legal Operations subgroup. In this role you’ll partner with stakeholders across the organization to scale, modernize, and continue to automate how our global legal team operates including driving the adoption of AI-powered tools and workflows. The Legal team supports Datadog’s rapid growth by providing a wide range of legal services across a highly dynamic technology company, from driving new business via contracts and compliance efforts, to protecting Datadog’s intellectual property. Datadog’s Legal team collaborates with virtually every team across the organization, from engineering to product to marketing.

  • Own and continuously improve legal processes end-to-end, partnering with legal and non-legal process owners to drive improvements, optimization, and automation
  • Liaise with technical and cross-functional teams to implement solutions, integrate systems, and troubleshoot issues reported by the legal team
  • Create and manage SOPs and collaborate with legal and non-legal colleagues on cross-functional projects
  • Analyze and use data, including AI-generated insights and dashboards, to drive initiatives, support forecasting and planning, and deliver reporting to legal leadership and other stakeholders
  • Manage technology used by the legal team (current tools include Brightflag, Salesforce, ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity) and become a superuser of new tools
  • Champion new systems and emerging AI capabilities
  • Support the legal team’s outside counsel operations 
  • Continuously cross-train across to operate as a flexible member of a shared services model, enabling coverage, resource-sharing, and consistent process standards

  • Familiar with program management tools and techniques, including breaking down tasks, roadmapping, assigning owners with timelines, and reporting
  • Genuinely passionate about technology, with hands-on experience evaluating or deploying AI and automation tools in a legal or business operations context
  • Able to move forward in times of ambiguity and imperfect knowledge, and comfortable acting as a change agent for new ways of working
  • An effective communicator and detail-oriented, able to translate technical or AI-related concepts for non-technical legal stakeholders
  • Someone with high integrity and strong judgment, including sound judgment about the appropriate and responsible use of AI with sensitive legal and business data

title: Indirect Tax Manager
description:
Datadog is seeking an Indirect Tax Manager to oversee U.S. sales and use tax compliance, support related audits, and coordinate VAT/GST obligations across our global entity portfolio. You will partner with external advisors and cross-functional teams to address evolving indirect tax requirements, strengthen controls, and embed tax considerations into business systems and processes. This role offers the opportunity to manage complex, multi-jurisdictional workstreams while helping scale a global indirect tax function. You will also expand your expertise across tax technology, e-invoicing, compliance operations, and international tax matters as Datadog continues to grow.

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

What You’ll Do:

  • Review U.S. multi-state sales and use tax filings prepared by the team, ensuring accuracy and alignment with established nexus and taxability positions
  • Support U.S. sales and use tax audits, notices, and inquiries by coordinating documentation, technical analysis, external advisors, and communications with tax authorities
  • Coordinate VAT/GST compliance and recovery activities across Datadog’s international entity portfolio, partnering with advisors across EMEA, APAC, and LATAM
  • Monitor changes in nexus, taxability, VAT/GST, e-invoicing, and e-reporting requirements, and communicate relevant impacts to internal stakeholders
  • Partner with Accounting, Revenue, Legal, Procurement, and Engineering to incorporate indirect tax requirements into billing systems, ERP configurations, controls, and new market or product initiatives
  • Develop and maintain process documentation, audit-readiness materials, workstream tracking, and SOX-aligned controls that support a scalable indirect tax function

Who You Are:

  • Experienced in progressive indirect tax roles within public accounting, an in-house tax function, or a combination of both
  • Knowledgeable in U.S. multi-state sales and use tax, including nexus analysis, taxability, compliance, and audit support
  • Familiar with international VAT/GST regimes and experienced coordinating compliance across multiple jurisdictions and external advisors
  • Experienced using tax determination and ERP systems; experience with Avalara and NetSuite is preferred
  • Able to manage multiple concurrent workstreams, analyze detailed financial information, and maintain accuracy in a fast-moving environment
  • A clear communicator who can translate technical indirect tax matters for Finance, Legal, and business stakeholders; experience with tax automation, AI-enabled process improvements, SOX environments, or relevant professional certifications is a plus

Datadog values people from all walks of life. We know not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That’s okay. If you’re passionate about technology and want to grow your experience, we encourage you to apply.

Benefits and Growth:

  • Expand your expertise across U.S. sales and use tax and international VAT/GST matters
  • Gain experience supporting a global, multi-entity tax function in a growing technology business
  • Partner with teams across Finance, Legal, Procurement, Revenue, and Engineering
  • Develop practical experience with tax technology, automation, e-invoicing, and systems implementation
  • Strengthen your capabilities in audit management, process design, internal controls, and cross-functional program delivery

title: HRIS Manager
description:
At Datadog, People Operations is more than just human resources—it’s a data-driven team dedicated to constantly improving the way we hire, develop, and support our most valuable asset: our people. Our People Operations team are strategic problem solvers who work closely with leadership and employees to ensure that Datadog keeps scaling smoothly and remains a great place to work. 

 

Datadog is seeking a HRIS Manager who will be responsible for managing and supporting projects within People Technology. This hands-on technical role demands excellent knowledge of HR business processes and methodologies along with a strong analytical and reporting background. 

A successful candidate will have a solid understanding of Workday and the ability to focus on one or more of the functional areas in People Operations. This will include the ability to assess systems and business processes, coordinate with peers, project managers, and management on impacts to other Datadog systems or business processes. You will play a critical role in the continued deployment of new functionality, developing solutions and enabling the continued growth of Datadog. 

 

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds, and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

What You’ll Do:

  • Own the end-to-end product lifecycle for your pod's systems and processes—from gathering requirements and designing solutions through testing, delivery, and adoption.
  • Serve as the Workday subject matter expert for your domain, advising stakeholders on configuration best practices, optimization opportunities, and governance.
  • Assess when Workday is the right tool and when a specialized third-party platform better serves the business. You'll partner with stakeholders on those decisions and own the requirements that follow.
  • Understand integration concepts well enough to make informed build-vs-buy decisions and clearly define requirements for our integrations team—you won't be building integrations, but you'll know why they're needed and what they need to do.
  • Design, build, and maintain custom Workday reports, dashboards, and calculated fields to surface the right data to the right people at the right time.
  • Partner cross-functionally with IT, Finance, Business Operations, and global People teams to align on requirements, recommend solutions, and drive delivery.
  • Identify and drive AI and automation opportunities within your domain—reducing manual work and increasing the intelligence of your systems.
  • Manage testing and quality assurance, including regression testing for system updates, new configurations, and third-party changes.
  • Create and maintain system documentation, change management materials, and training resources that drive adoption across the People team and the broader organization.
  • Manage projects independently—scoping, communicating, and delivering with sound judgment about when to escalate.

Who You Are:

  • 7+ years of hands-on HRIS experience with deep Workday knowledge across one or more functional areas. Workday Pro certification is a plus.
  • A systems thinker who evaluates the full People tech ecosystem—not just what's possible in Workday, but what's the right solution for the business, whether that's native configuration, a third-party tool, or a smarter process.
  • Technically fluent enough to understand integrations, data flows, and downstream impacts—so you can make good decisions and write clear requirements, even when someone else does the building.
  • Skilled at translating ambiguous business problems into clear, scalable HRIS solutions. You ask the right questions before writing a single business process step.
  • Experienced in end-to-end Workday implementation and enhancement work, including project management, stakeholder communication, and change management.
  • Knowledgeable in Workday security model design and configuration, with an understanding of how security decisions affect user experience, compliance, and downstream systems.
  • Curious about AI, automation, and emerging HR technology—and proactive about finding opportunities to apply them.
  • Comfortable managing multiple priorities in a fast-moving environment, adapting when requirements shift, and escalating with good judgment.

Datadog values people from all walks of life. We understand not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That's okay. If you’re passionate about technology and want to grow your skills, we encourage you to apply.

title: Head of Competitive Intelligence
location: New York, New York, USA; San Francisco, California, USA
description:
Datadog is building a product-led Competitive Intelligence function to help inform product strategy, roadmap prioritization, positioning, and competitive readiness.

As the Head of Competitive Intelligence you will build and lead the CompIntel function across priority competitors and adjacent market opportunities. You will translate competitor product evolution, technical capabilities, launches, pricing value, customer sentiment, analyst narratives, and ecosystem shifts into actionable insights for Product, GTM, Sales Engineering, Customer Success, Technical Advocacy, and leadership.

In this highly technical, hands-on leadership role, you should understand how observability products are implemented, where workflows differ, what technical claims are credible, and how product gaps translate into customer impact.

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds, and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

What You'll Do: 

  • Own the recurring competitive radar for Datadog’s priority competitor set, including taxonomy, source standards, evidence quality, and update cadence.
  • Produce competitive deep dives, feature-gap analyses, early-warning briefs, and opportunity assessments tied to specific product domains and leadership questions.
  • Translate CompIntel findings into roadmap recommendations, product differentiation hypotheses, and Product-facing decision guidance.
  • Build and maintain a central CompIntel repository with competitor profiles, source notes, comparison frameworks, evidence logs, and decision-ready briefs.
  • Convert validated findings into GTM-ready handoffs for battlecards, objection handling, strategic deal narratives, and field enablement.
  • Synthesize signals from Product, Engineering, Sales Engineering, Customer Success, field teams, technical communities, Advocacy programs, win/loss, customer feedback, analyst research, public competitor materials, and CABs.
  • Partner with Product Management to frame competitive questions, identify decision criteria, and connect findings to roadmap and prioritization discussions.
  • Partner with Technical Advocacy to incorporate practitioner, customer, technical-market, community, event, and CAB signal into competitive analysis.
  • Present concise, credible recommendations to Product leadership and Product + GTM forums.
  • Maintain source transparency, legal compliance, ethical research practices, and auditable methods across competitive research workflows.
  • Lead a small, high-impact team of CompIntel analysts and engineers.

Who You Are: 

  • You have 8+ years of experience in competitive intelligence, technical product strategy, product management, market intelligence, strategic technical research, or related enterprise software work.
  • You have strong technical fluency in one or more of the following areas: observability, cloud infrastructure, security, developer tooling, distributed systems or enterprise SaaS platforms.
  • You are comfortable reading technical documentation, changelogs, release notes, architecture diagrams, product announcements, and public competitor materials.
  • You can distinguish credible technical differentiation from surface-level claims.
  • You can synthesize technical, commercial, customer, and market evidence into clear recommendations.
  • You have strong executive writing skills and can produce concise memos, structured briefs, comparison frameworks, and leadership-ready recommendations.
  • You can influence Product, Engineering, Marketing, Sales Engineering, Sales, Customer Success, and leadership stakeholders without direct authority.
  • You are comfortable working in ambiguous environments where the function, taxonomy, operating cadence, and stakeholder model need to be built from the ground up.
  • You understand legal, ethical, and compliance considerations in competitive intelligence gathering.

Bonus Points: 

  • Experience in observability, cloud infrastructure, security, developer tooling, platform engineering, or technical enterprise SaaS.
  • Experience supporting Product Management or product strategy through technical analysis, roadmap inputs, customer evidence, or market intelligence.
  • Experience building a competitive intelligence program, research repository, competitor taxonomy, or recurring market-monitoring process.
  • Familiarity with SCIP ethics guidance, evidence governance, source transparency, and legally approved research methods.
  • Experience translating technical findings into GTM-ready enablement materials without overstating claims.

title: Group Product Manager - Bring Your Own Cloud
description:
We're on a mission to build the best platform in the world for engineers to understand and scale their systems, applications, and teams. We operate at high scale—trillions of data points per day—allowing for seamless collaboration and problem-solving among Dev, Ops and Security teams globally for tens of thousands of companies. Our engineering culture values pragmatism, honesty, and simplicity to solve hard problems the right way.

 

The Team:

As organizations rapidly invest in AI applications and build out AI labs, telemetry volumes are growing exponentially and costs are becoming unpredictable. From LLM interactions to agentic workflows, AI systems generate unpredictable streams of logs, driving up costs and making it harder to maintain efficient observability. These challenges are critical for organizations in regulated industries with strict data residency requirements, where data must remain within controlled environments. Datadog’s Bring Your Own Cloud (BYOC) team is reimagining what observability and security look like at petabyte scale in the AI era.

 

The Opportunity:

The Group Product Manager - Bring Your Own Cloud (BYOC) role is responsible for defining and bringing to market the next generation of telemetry analytics and insights capabilities in an AI-first environment. This role is highly technical and creative in nature as you will envision novel ways to enable customers to cost-effectively explore, analyze and report over petabytes of data through a welcoming and easy-to-use interface. You will partner with various teams to take advantage of BitsAI capabilities and surface critical insights on volume usage and retention for popular use cases.

 

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

 

What You’ll Do:

 

  • Lead and grow a team of product managers focused on Datadog’s BYOC Program
  • Define the vision, strategy, and product roadmap for BYOC and make it immediately valuable to customers in an AI-first environment
  • Gather insights from customers, partners, and internal data to become an expert on how customers want to store, analyze, and report on data for long term needs
  • Work closely with Datadog’s BYOC, Log Management, BitsAI, and Platform teams to identify opportunities and build ingest, index and search capabilities for petabyte scale 
  • Make it easy for customers to onboard new workloads and products within Datadog onto the BYOC platform
  • Recommend and launch new offerings with BYOC based on use cases for Security and Compliance
  • Partner with Marketing and other GTM teams to generate awareness and drive adoption of Datadog’s BYOC offering
  • Present to leading industry experts and analysts such as Gartner, Forrester and IDC to influence the market research teams and solicit feedback to guide roadmap
  • Guide Product Solution Architects to build pre-validated architectures on getting started with BYOC for specific use cases and industry verticals

 

Who You Are: 

  • A Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science or Engineering or equivalent experience
  • 7+ years of experience in B2B SaaS Product Management, including 2+ years managing other product managers
  • At least 3+ years of experience with databases, data warehouses, SQL concepts & language, BI products, and/or distributed systems
  • Hands on experience using multiple services from one or more of the major cloud providers (AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud)
  • Demonstrated track record of working with executives and engineers alike
  • Prior experience with Snowflake, Databricks, Splunk, or ClickHouse is a strong plus
  • MBA is a strong plus

title: Global Safety & Security Manager
description:
The Global Safety & Security Team falls under the Operations Team that runs many day-to-day operational functions that help keep our employees safe, happy and productive. We work closely with leadership and employees to ensure that Datadog continues to scale rapidly, yet smoothly and remains a fantastic place to work.

We’re seeking an experienced team member to join our growing global team and play a critical role in keeping Datadogs and its assets safe and secure. You will work directly with the Global Head of Global Safety & Security and cross-functional teams to support safety and security operations across the enterprise. Ideal candidates will be passionate about leadership, security operations, building programs, workplace health and safety, project management, customer service and collaboration. This position is based in our Sydney or Singapore office and will require domestic and international travel. The role will focus particularly on developing our safety compliance, security program development and maturity, incident, investigations and crisis management programs.

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

What You’ll Do:

  • Manage day-to-day global safety and security operations for Datadog’s regional offices  in APAC, including its co-working locations and assist with global safety and security initiatives. 
  • Providing ad-hoc coverage for the EMEA and AMER region may be required at the discretion of the Global Head of Global Safety & Security.
  • Oversee a variety of responsibilities, including investigations, health and safety compliance, security risk management, travel safety, event security, budgeting, crisis management, emergency response, property loss management and global safety and security system management. Enforce Datadog’s security policies and regulations regionally.
  • Document and disseminate security protocols under the guidance of the Head of Global Safety & Security. Develop regional policies, technical security solutions, safety protocols, emergency preparedness training and liaise with local law enforcement in individual offices.
  • Collaborate with various teams, including Office Operations, Real Estate, IT, Legal, Events and People. Maintain regular communication with stakeholders to ensure alignment on global safety and security initiatives and ensure all teams are trained on emergency plans and incident response protocols.
  • Execute daily operations and strategic initiatives for workplace safety and security, contract security personnel management, and response to incidents in Datadog offices.
  • Identify long-term needs in terms of organizational structure, policies/procedures and capital enhancements. Develop strategic plans to obtain executive approval, define objectives, secure resources and execute key milestones.
  • Provide assessments and briefings to leadership, ensuring understanding of corrective actions, their impact and urgency.
  • Facilitate tabletop exercises for regional offices focused on emergency preparedness, crisis management and resilience.

Who You Are:

  • Experienced in managing safety and security operations, ideally within a fast-paced technology environment, with a focus on developing security and safety programs and incident response plans.
  • Skilled in managing all aspects of a physical security program, including but not limited to Executive Protection, Event Security and Travel Security.
  • Experienced in building and growing regional and global safety and security programs to scale with organizational needs.
  • Knowledgeable about global technical security monitoring systems, with experience reviewing architectural plans and planning physical security design.
  • Familiarity with enterprise physical security risk management principles, including conducting security and safety risk assessments and implementing mitigation strategies.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills to effectively convey security information across all levels of the organization with specific focus to executives.
  • Strong vendor management capabilities, with a track record of managing and coordinating with external security vendors.
  • 8+ years of experience in corporate physical security and safety roles within a global security environment, with specific expertise in Asia Pacific (APAC) regions.

As a Front Desk Associate on Datadog’s Office Operations team, you will help create a welcoming, safe, and productive workplace for employees, candidates, visitors, and partners. You will support both front-of-house operations and the day-to-day facilities needs of the office, including reception, building access, mail and packages, workplace maintenance, supplies, vendor coordination, and employee events. title: FP&A Analyst
description:
About Datadog:

Datadog is the essential monitoring and security platform for cloud applications. We bring together end-to-end traces, metrics, and logs to make your applications, infrastructure, and third-party services entirely observable. These capabilities help businesses secure their systems, avoid downtime, and ensure customers are getting the best user experience.

The Team:

The Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) team analyzes company financial data (revenue, customers, headcount, expenses, etc.) in order to support the business’ growth and success. Within FP&A, the R&D Finance team enables the financial strategy behind Datadog’s Engineering and Product organizations. We partner directly with technical leadership to drive decision-making around our most critical investments.

The Opportunity:

As a part of the R&D Finance team, this person will be key in supporting our product and engineering leadership team. Reporting to the Senior Manager, you will help create our annual budget and financial targets and work with operational leaders to support execution against our goals. Your work will be highly cross-functional and strategic, and you will play a pivotal role in connecting the dots across the organization through a financial lens, in order to help ensure operational alignment and inform decision making.

What You’ll Do:

  • Partner with senior business leaders to manage their departmental budgets on a regular basis, including but not limited to the company’s co-founder and CTO 
  • Manage financial forecasts and analytics, which include data across revenue, customers, product, company expenses, and headcount / workforce.
  • Help manage significant portions of the company’s spend, including but not limited to AI and GPU spend across the company.
  • Work on trend, ROI, and profitability analyses on both product and customer levels to support data-driven decision making
  • Work with finance management on quarterly Board materials, including coordination and consolidation across stakeholders
  • Assist in planning and budgeting cycles, ensuring consistency in tools, templates, and processes across the organization
  • Work on ad hoc projects and strategic initiatives for senior management, which may include assessing potential acquisition opportunities and/or negotiations with strategic partners like cloud vendors
  • Become proficient with various financial planning and business intelligence (BI) tools, including but not limited to Pigment, Tableau, and Metabase

Who You Are:

  • 2+ years of professional experience in FP&A / Strategic Finance, Corporate Finance, Investment Banking, and/or other related field
  • Bachelor's degree in finance, accounting, business, or economics
  • Mastery of Excel and PowerPoint with proven experience in building financial models and managing complex data
  • You are a clear, concise communicator and team player with a humble mindset and ‘can-do’ attitude 

Bonus Points:

  • Solid understanding of Pigment is a plus, but not required
  • Experience in or understanding of a consumption-based software business model
  • Proficiency in use of AI tools (e.g. ChatGPT, Claude)

Benefits and Growth: 

  • Generous and competitive benefits package
  • New hire stock equity (RSUs) and employee stock purchase plan
  • Continuous career development and pathing opportunities 
  • Product training to develop an in-depth understanding of our product and space
  • Friendly and inclusive workplace culture

title: Head of Regulated Industries, Customer Success
location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As Head of Regulated Industries – Customer Success at Anthropic, you'll lead the Success teams responsible for our most complex Financial Services (FSI) and Healthcare & Life Sciences (HCLS) customers. Think banks, insurers, asset and wealth managers and financial data providers; health systems, hospitals and payers; and pharmaceutical, biotech and life-sciences organizations. You'll directly coach and develop a team of Customer Success Managers who drive value across the full product portfolio (Claude Platform, Claude Code, Claude Cowork). These are organizations where deployment runs through compliance, procurement, security review, model risk and legal before it reaches an end user.

You'll partner day to day with the Regulated Industries sales organization so that customers experience one Anthropic from first conversation to production. You'll turn what works at one regulated customer into a methodology that works at the next. That means success plans that anticipate the governance gates. Executive programs that reach the CIO, CISO, CRO and compliance leaders who decide whether Claude gets deployed. Expansion plays that survive long procurement cycles.

You’ll inherit a partially formed team, spanning individual contributors and managers. You'll hire and run the initial team yourself. As the book expands you'll continue to add managers underneath you and manage through them. We're looking for someone who has already led a success business in regulated environments and wants to build the operating model that lets it scale.

Responsibilities:

  • Directly manage and develop a team of Customer Success Managers covering Financial Services and Healthcare & Life Sciences enterprise accounts — the Regulated Industries book — across all Anthropic products.

  • Own the hiring plan for the team, including sourcing for regulated-industry experience, onboarding and ramp design; later, hire and develop team leads and shift to managing through them.

  • Coach the team on success practice specific to regulated customers. That includes navigating compliance, procurement, security and model-risk reviews; building champions across business, technology and risk functions; change management under strict controls; and value realization across consumption and seat-based models.

  • Drive team accountability to core CS metrics: expansion (consumption growth, adoption), customer health, retention (NRR) and customer satisfaction (CSAT).

  • Join strategic customer engagements and escalations, with executive presence in front of CIOs, CISOs, chief risk and compliance officers, heads of business lines and board-level sponsors.

  • Build and refine the regulated-industries success methodology. Success planning frameworks that map the governance path to consumption; QBR and executive-briefing templates; security and compliance readiness playbooks; reference architectures and expansion playbooks that transfer from one regulated customer to the next.

  • Partner closely with the Regulated Industries sales organization to align on account strategy, set clear ownership between AEs and CSMs, and manage handoffs so long deployment cycles don't stall between teams.

  • Collaborate with Product, Engineering, Security, Legal and Marketing to advocate for regulated customers' needs and translate field signal into product direction.

  • Establish an AI-first, innovation-focused team culture; improve team processes and deepen hands-on product expertise.

  • Conduct regular 1:1s, performance reviews and career development planning for direct reports.

  • Own portfolio-level planning and forecasting, including renewal-risk mitigation and consumption development across the regulated book.

  • Serve as the escalation point for at-risk customers and complex situations in the team's portfolio.

  • Develop advocacy assets for regulated customers: case studies, references and reference architectures that can be shared within compliance constraints.

  • Champion responsible AI deployment practices with customers and represent Anthropic's values in every customer interaction.

You may be a good fit if you have:

  • 10+ years in customer success, account management or customer-facing roles, with 5+ years of front-line management experience; 2+ years of experience managing managers.

  • Direct experience driving a Success business with regulated customers — financial services, healthcare and life sciences, or comparable regulated sectors. That means working through compliance, procurement, security review, risk and legal gates and consensus-building across executives to get to consumption.

  • A proven track record of managing and building customer success teams in SaaS, API or AI/ML companies.

  • Experience managing enterprise portfolios, including accounts with multi-million dollar annual contract values and deployment cycles measured in quarters, not weeks.

  • Demonstrated ability to drive outcomes in organizations with many decision-makers and no single owner, and to coach a team to do the same.

  • A strong understanding of both consumption-based and seat-based business models, with a record of driving adoption, expansion and value realization across them.

  • Experience developing repeatable frameworks, playbooks or enablement programs that other teams adopted independently of you.

  • Technical fluency to understand AI/ML products and the deployment, data and security considerations regulated customers raise. 

  • Working knowledge of the regulatory and compliance frameworks these customers operate under e.g. HIPAA, FDA and healthcare data-security requirements

  • Strong executive presence with both business and risk-side leaders. Represents Anthropic credibly in a CISO or model-risk conversation as well as a CFO one.

  • Strong business acumen: articulating value, calculating ROI and driving customer business outcomes.

  • The ability to balance strategic thinking with tactical execution, and to context-switch between coaching, customer engagement and operational planning.

  • A knack for bringing order to chaos and an enthusiastic "roll up your sleeves" mentality

  • Passion for responsible AI development and for helping customers transform their businesses with cutting-edge technology.



The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. 

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$320,000—$350,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. title: Head of Recruiting, Communications, Brand, & Marketing
description:

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic's Communications, Brand, and Marketing teams shape how people inside the company and around the world understand AI, its risks, and its benefits. They move fast, often through moments that make headlines. We're looking for a recruiting leader to run the team that hires for them.

In this role you will lead a team of experienced recruiters and be the main recruiting partner to the leaders of these functions and their operations partners. The team is seasoned, and each recruiter brings deep context on the business. From day one you have two first priorities: the team you manage and the leaders you support. You might spend one hour coaching a recruiter through a hard search and the next working with a senior leader on how their organization needs to grow.

Key responsibilities

  • Lead, coach, and retain a team of senior recruiters, with a focus on fast and timely feedback
  • Build deep trust with the leaders of Communications, Brand, and Marketing. Learn what they need, raise hiring risks early, and push back when the plan and the market don't match.
  • Run a tight operation. Own headcount plans, pipeline data, and reporting, and keep them accurate enough that leaders and operations partners can plan from them.
  • Use data to show where each search stands, where it is stuck, and what it will take to close.
  • Work with the operations partners for these teams on headcount, planning, and priorities, and treat them as true partners.
  • Set one consistent process across the team: how a search runs, how interviews are structured, how data stays clean, and how recruiters use our systems and Claude workflows.
  • Hire recruiters onto your own team, including specialists in communications and brand hiring.
  • Partner with Compensation, Finance, People Partners, and Recruiting Operations so that candidates and hiring teams get a clear, fair process.

title: Head of Policy Design, Societal Harms
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic's Safeguards organization builds the policies, evaluations, and detection and enforcement systems that define and hold the limits on how Claude can be used. In this role, you'll lead our policy design team, managing the teams responsible for radicalization, child safety, user well-being, harmful manipulation, and election integrity, among other harm areas.

The team is responsible for understanding and defining the risks that come with engaging with Claude, how those risks materialize in the real world, and the mitigations needed to prevent them. As the manager, you'll work with your team to draw the boundaries between what is and is not allowed, then partner with research, product, and engineering to build the right interventions. Mitigating these harms takes the whole stack: the values and judgment trained into the model itself, the policies and detection systems we enforce on top of it, and the interventions we build into our products. More capable models, new product surfaces, and new user behaviors will keep testing these boundaries, so the team's policies have to keep pace.

You'll work closely with product to develop and iterate on the strategy and vision for how our safety layers fit together, and with your team and cross-functional partners to decide which mitigations make the most sense and how to implement them. You'll also coordinate policy decisions across the portfolio: ensuring they're made with the right stakeholders in the room, tracked over time, and applied consistently across harm areas and product surfaces.

This is a leadership role for someone who combines expertise in the harm areas themselves with fluency in how frontier models are actually developed and deployed, and who does their best work across team boundaries. You'll spend as much time developing the leads who own each harm area as you will on the policy questions themselves.

*Important context for this role: some of the work involves exposure to explicit content, including material of a sexual, violent, or psychologically disturbing nature.

  • Partner with engineering, data science, product, legal, and research across the model development cycle so consumer harms considerations are represented from training through launch, on every surface where Claude is deployed

  • A track record of exceptional cross-team collaboration: building durable working relationships with teams you don't control, and getting to shared decisions where ownership is genuinely distributed

  • Working understanding of how frontier models are developed and deployed — the training and fine-tuning cycle, evaluations, and launch processes — and how different model environments (consumer products, APIs, agentic tools) change both risk and the mitigations available

  • Experience translating policy positions into mechanisms that can be enforced and measured, and communicating the reasoning to technical and non-technical audiences, including executives

  • Sound judgment in ambiguous, high-consequence decisions, and comfort making a call and escalating appropriately on incomplete information

location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. About the role

Anthropic trains and serves frontier AI models on some of the largest and most diverse accelerator fleets in the world, and the hardware those models run on is one of the most direct levers we have on capability, cost, and reliability. Our Hardware Systems team owns the system-level architecture of that compute — from the package boundary out through boards, racks, interconnect, power, cooling, and the datacenter interface.

We're hiring senior hardware systems architects and technical leads who can work broadly across the hardware stack and go deep where it's needed, and who have the judgment to make and own directional calls — what to build, what to buy, what to co-design with a partner. You'll set architecture, write the specs that partners and internal teams build against, and own the validation and qualification strategy that proves the result.

The skillsets we need span power, cooling, mechanical, interconnect, signal integrity, data and control plane, system management, reliability and serviceability — applied across networking, compute, storage, and accelerator systems.

You'll work closely with our ML performance, infrastructure software, supply chain, and datacenter teams, and directly with hardware vendors and partners across the stack. And because this is Anthropic, you'll have Claude as a genuine collaborator — we expect this team to push on what AI-assisted hardware design and review can look like.

Key responsibilities

  • Own system path-finding and architecture for your domain across the breadth of compute Anthropic deploys — from concept and requirements through spec, design review, and deployment — and act as a reviewer and thought partner across the others.
  • Write and own high-level requirements and specifications — system, board, interface, rack — that partners and internal teams build against.
  • Review partner and vendor designs against our requirements, make the build / buy / co-design calls with supply chain and partnership teams, and surface misalignment or schedule risk early enough to act on it.
  • Drive the interconnect and networking architecture that ties our systems together — scale-up and scale-out fabrics, NICs and switches, optics, and topology.
  • Drive board-, chassis-, and system-level architecture with our partners — major component placement, PCB architecture, connector and cable design, and power and thermal budgeting — at the chassis, rack, and data-hall level.
  • Develop performance simulations, hardware models, and "what-if" scenarios to evaluate and choose between candidate hardware architectures.
  • Define validation, bring-up, and qualification strategy for new platforms — including the telemetry and reliability targets they need to hit in the fleet — and track the technology roadmaps and vendor landscape that shape what we deploy in the short and long term.
  • Partner with ML performance and infrastructure software teams so hardware decisions land well for the workloads that actually run on them.
  • Help shape how hardware engineering operates at Anthropic — develop and apply AI-assisted approaches to design, spec review, and validation; establish review forums, spec standards, and partner engagement.

Minimum qualifications

  • Deep, hands-on expertise in at least one core hardware-systems domain (e.g., interconnect, power, thermal) for large-scale compute or networking systems.
  • Experience owning hardware system architecture at scale — machine, rack, row, and cluster — and authoring specifications and requirements.
  • Experience taking hardware from architecture through bring-up and high-volume production deployment.
  • Experience working with external hardware vendors and partners — reviewing their designs and holding them to a specification.
  • Ability to reason about trade-offs across adjacent hardware domains (e.g., interconnect ↔ power ↔ thermal ↔ mechanical) rather than within a single one.
  •  Track record of technical leadership — owning directional decisions and their consequences, and driving alignment across teams and partners.
  • Comfort operating with high autonomy and limited process in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment.
  • Strong written communication — you'll write specs and reviews that many teams depend on.

Preferred qualifications

  • 8+ years in hardware systems architecture or engineering for hyperscale, HPC, AI/ML, or high-end networking platforms.
  • Experience with AI accelerator systems (GPU, TPU, or other custom ASIC platforms) and their scale-up / scale-out fabrics.
  • Familiarity with the chip-package-system interface and co-design.
  • Experience establishing a new function, program, or engineering practice.
  • Comfort working with — and curiosity about pushing — AI tools as part of an engineering workflow.
  • Degree in EE, CE, ME, CS, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • Depth in one or more of:
    • High-speed SerDes, PCIe/CXL, Ethernet/InfiniBand, and optical interconnect.
    • BMC and platform firmware, hardware root of trust, and secure boot.
    • 48V/HVDC power delivery and direct liquid cooling.
    • Fleet-scale reliability engineering and RAS architecture.
    • Signal and power integrity.

Representative projects

  • Define the scale-up and scale-out interconnect architecture for a next-generation training platform, from link budget and topology through switch / NIC / optics selection and the bring-up and validation plan.
  • Architect the management and control plane for a new hardware system: BMC and host control, power / reset sequencing, secure boot and attestation, and the telemetry surface the fleet needs.
  • Own the rack-level power and thermal architecture for a liquid-cooled accelerator rack, and the interface spec between that rack and the datacenter that hosts it.
  • Build the reliability model and RAS strategy for a multi-thousand-node fleet — failure budgets, derating policy, telemetry requirements, and serviceability targets — and drive the design changes that hit them.
  • Run the technical evaluation of a partner's proposed system design against our requirements, write up where it falls short, and drive the changes end to end.
  • Prototype an AI-assisted workflow for partner design review and spec consistency checking, and put it to work on a live platform.

Foragers is a new Field Services team within our physical infrastructure organization. We're the boots on the ground for Anthropic's physical infrastructure: the people who get hardware into racks, gear commissioned, and sites handed over. The team is being stood up now, so early hires shape how we operate. This role is the lab-focused counterpart to our traveling field engineers. Instead of covering sites across the country, you own our Bay Area hardware labs from end to end.

Your mission is to ensure our hardware labs are functional, useful, and ready to support the growing number of teams and projects that need access to physical hardware. You’d own what shows up, how it’s powered, cooled, cabled, tracked, set up, and made functional. This includes both standard hardware (think typical accelerator setups) and more specialized ones like ensuring our security teams have access to all the right headers and other hardware instrumentation on the machines.

Understanding and anticipating the needs of the various teams that rely on the labs will be another critical part of this role. You’ll be expected to take a lot of ownership and initiative over the lab and what’s in it, including reaching out to partner teams to figure out what they’d need in the future and making sure it’s there before it starts to block them. You’d be the first dedicated lab manager, so part of this role will include shaping it to scale from our current lab to much larger ones.

  • Run the physical lab across both sites: receiving and staging, rack-and-stack, cabling, power distribution and load planning, cooling, floor layout

  • Handle physical access, asset auditing, and lifecycle tracking for hardware that is expensive and sometimes pre-release
  • Write it down: build the playbooks and lightweight tooling (inventory, remote power, console access) so remote teams can use the lab without pinging you for every step

  • Working knowledge of server hardware and its management plane: BMC/IPMI/Redfish, BIOS/UEFI configuration, serial console, PXE/network boot, firmware updates
  • Enough Linux and networking (VLANs, DHCP, DNS, basic switch config) to take a bare machine to a state a remote engineer can use
  • Have managed vendors, contractors, quotes, and freight for physical equipment
  • Comfortable and safe with power tools, bench power supplies, and a wiring or rack elevation diagram
  • Work independently with minimal supervision , and know when to ask

  • Experience with DCIM or asset-management tooling (NetBox, ServiceNow, etc.)
  • Bought hard-to-source or specialty hardware and dealt with the compliance and logistics that come with it

title: Global Real Estate Construction Manager
description:
