Proven ability to influence senior leaders and drive cross-functional change without formal authority. Experience translating ambiguous talent philosophies into scalable tools, frameworks, and operating mechanisms. Strong business acumen and organizational judgment, with the ability to connect talent decisions to company outcomes. Excitement for reimagining talent management in an AI-native world. As Notion scales across products and jurisdictions, this role exists to make compliance, close, audits, and tax data more accurate, scalable, and audit-ready. You’ll own recurring sales and use tax, VAT/GST, business tax, registrations, notices, reconciliations, and related controls, while building exposure to income tax compliance and reporting. Establish a reliable reconciliation and exception workflow across billing, tax engines, filings, payments, and the general ledger, escalating issues clearly and early. Use AI-enabled workflows and data tools to investigate variances, quality-check work papers, and improve documentation while preserving human review and controls. Make tax operations more scalable and audit-ready by strengthening controls, process documentation, evidence, handoffs, audit support, and SOX walkthrough readiness. Become a trusted partner to Accounting, Revenue, Billing, Product, Engineering, Data, and Customer Experience—and contribute to income tax compliance and reporting with guidance from experienced teammates. Hands-on experience with indirect tax compliance or operations, especially U.S. sales and use tax, VAT/GST, business taxes, or other non-income-based taxes; this is the foundation for owning Notion’s recurring global work. Experience preparing accurate reconciliations, journal entries, filings, payments, and audit-ready work papers, with the ability to connect activity across source systems and the general ledger. Strong operational judgment: you manage recurring deadlines, investigate exceptions, keep documentation organized, escalate issues promptly, and drive assigned work through completion. Clear written and verbal communication, with a collaborative approach to working across Finance, Accounting, business teams, and external advisors. Curiosity and learning agility, including willingness to build income-tax capability and demonstrated AI fluency—using AI to analyze data, investigate variances, improve documentation, perform quality checks, or automate repeatable workflows while validating outputs and protecting sensitive information. About the Role: Notion has a very successful "land and expand" business model; our customers start using Notion for free, upgrade over time as they expand their teams, and embrace increasingly sophisticated use cases. Often, these users and champions are different than the person who has enterprise purchasing authority. The Demand Generation team serves as a dot-connecter across sales, marketing, and operation teams to identify, engage, and convert decision makers at our target mid market and enterprise companies. In this role, you will partner with demand generation teammates and sales stakeholders to ideate and execute in-person events, designed to help open, accelerate, and close business. As a Field Marketing Manager, you will own and execute field events that are Notion-hosted, third party, co-partnered, and ancillary to third party events. This strategic position focuses on driving pipeline that meaningfully contribute to Notion's bottom line. This role can be based in either San Francisco or New York City. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. We’re looking for someone who’s excited to work alongside the team during those days. What You'll Achieve: Delight Notion customers and prospects , with a guest-first approach to creating field events and experiences that bring the Notion brand and product to life. Own end-to-end planning, execution, and measurement of field programs to support our AMER Sales team - encompassing executive experiences, large-format educational events, trade shows, and co-sponsored activations with partners. Manage all event logistics , production, venue sourcing, budget tracking, marketing campaigns, sales enablement, content development, and audience acquisition. Leverage quantitative and qualitative insights to make recommendations on how we invest in field events to drive incremental business impact. Partner closely with Sales and broader Marketing team to align events and audiences to objectives for top accounts and craft tailored programs that nurture those accounts Partner with our Operation and BizTech teams to manage and better utilize our go-to-market systems Skills You'll Need to Bring: 4-5+ years of related marketing experience. You don’t need to be an AI expert, but you’re curious and willing to adopt AI tools to work smarter and deliver better results. You're a creative problem-solver who doesn't wait for a perfect playbook. You've built field events from scratch, and you're energized by figuring out what works in new territory. You have a bias for action and experimentation. You'd rather test and learn than wait for consensus, and you know how to balance scrappiness with strategic thinking. You're a strong cross-functional collaborator. You know how to work with sales, ops, and creative teams — and you can align people around a shared goal without needing authority to do it. You're pipeline-obsessed. You understand how your programs connect to revenue and can speak credibly about pipeline contribution, not just top-of-funnel metrics. Nice to Haves: Experience in a fast-paced, B2B tech environment You're a Notion user and understand our value to businesses Salesforce, Marketo experience Notion is committed to providing highly competitive cash compensation, equity, and benefits. About the Role: Notion is looking for a Forward Deployed Engineer focused on migrations to join our growing team in India. You will help deliver complex, production-grade data migrations, integrations, and automations for customers across APAC. This is initially an internally focused, hands-on engineering role. You will partner closely with regional Forward Deployed Engineers, who own customer discovery, solution architecture, stakeholder communication, risk management, and final customer validation. You will own the behind-the-scenes technical execution layer from feasibility assessment and implementation through testing, production rollout, QA, reconciliation, reporting, and operational handoff. You will work across multiple customer environments and source systems, often with incomplete requirements, imperfect data, and real-world constraints. Success requires strong engineering fundamentals, sound judgment, careful validation, and the ability to turn one-off delivery work into reusable tools and repeatable playbooks. As a founding engineer in India, you will help build a new regional engineering capability from the ground up. You will create migration infrastructure, standards, and reusable tooling used by FDEs across APAC, while establishing practices that can scale globally. The role offers an opportunity to become a technical authority for production migration delivery, shaping how Notion approaches reliability, validation, and operational quality across complex customer environments. As the team grows, the role may also expand toward customer-facing FDE work, technical leadership, or a deeper engineering path, depending on business needs and demonstrated capability. What You'll Achieve: Own the technical execution layer after customer requirements, scope, and solution architecture have been established with the regional FDE. Contribute to feasibility assessment, estimation, implementation planning, and risk identification while the regional FDE remains accountable for customer discovery, scope, architecture, stakeholder communication, and final acceptance. Apply a repeatable migration lifecycle covering source inventory and sampling, scope and pruning decisions, compatibility and degradation assessment, transformation design, pilot or dry run, user acceptance testing, production cutover, reconciliation, remediation, hypercare, and documented handoff. Translate approved customer and regional FDE requirements into clear technical designs, implementation plans, test strategies, runbooks, and delivery estimates. Build production-quality migration utilities, backend services, data pipelines, integrations, and automations using Python, SQL, APIs, databases, and cloud infrastructure. Investigate source-system behavior, data quality issues, permissions, rate limits, authentication constraints, and edge cases, then recommend practical solutions. Design and validate permissions, ownership, and inheritance mappings against the approved migration plan. Make unsupported or ambiguous access requirements explicit, obtain the required decision or approval, and preserve evidence of validation. Design migrations for reliability, scale, security, observability, idempotency, failure recovery, and safe reruns. Execute migrations only through approved environments, devices, accounts, and tooling. Follow least-privilege access, customer-specific security and data-residency requirements, and approved handling procedures. Do not store customer data in unmanaged local or external systems, and escalate privacy, security, or sovereignty concerns before execution. Build validation and reconciliation frameworks that provide clear evidence of migration completeness, accuracy, and exceptions. Debug failures across application code, infrastructure, customer data, third-party systems, and the Notion platform, then drive issues through resolution. Manage multiple implementation workstreams, dependencies, and priorities while communicating scope, progress, risks, and trade-offs clearly. Surface scope changes, unsupported requirements, timeline risks, and material effort increases early. Document assumptions and trade-offs, and escalate with options and a recommended path rather than silently absorbing additional work. Maintain an auditable record of scope, decisions, risks, approvals, validation evidence, and customer acceptance criteria in the agreed shared workspace or channel. Convert repeated delivery patterns into reusable components, automation, documentation, and playbooks that improve speed, quality, and cost over time. Bring field learnings back to Notion's Product and Engineering teams as actionable platform feedback and technical requirements. Skills You'll Need to Bring: 3 to 6 years of hands-on experience in backend engineering, data engineering, integration engineering, implementation engineering, technical consulting, solutions engineering, or a similar technical role. Strong hands-on Python development experience. Working experience with Node.js, JavaScript, or TypeScript. Partner with Data Engineering on the definitions and data contracts that let finance metrics tie cleanly to source systems, and hold the line when teams drift Drive ITGC workstreams across in-scope financial systems: logical access and segregation of duties, change management, SDLC and CI/CD pipelines, job scheduling, and data interfaces. You understand how ITGC reliance determines what auditors will accept from automated controls and system-generated reports, can tell a key control from a non-key one, know where ITACs fit alongside ITGCs, and have been through remediation and audit cycles rather than only reading about them AI-native operating mindset; this is a core requirement for this role. About The Role Notion is reimagining how customers adopt, expand, and realize value from software in an AI-native world. You’ll work at the intersection of localization quality, training implementation, and program management , collaborating with Localization, Partner Enablement, Customer Education, vendors, and language specialists. You’ll help turn translation feedback, learner experience issues, and regional quality needs into practical improvements across training content, quizzes, LMS setup, and repeatable localization workflows. The ideal candidate combines native-level Japanese language expertise with a deep understanding of what effective education looks like in the Japanese market. What You'll Achieve Own and apply Japanese localization QA standards across training content, including checking for accuracy, clarity, tone, terminology, and cultural nuance Support development of glossaries, style guides, QA checklists, review processes, and localization assets Become a go-to partner for translation questions related to Notion-specific concepts, product terminology, and training context Support QA of technical implementation in eLearning authoring tools and LMS environments (course files, quizzes, answer selections) Coordinate across Customer Education, Partner Enablement, Localization, and vendors to align on priorities, timelines, translation progress, and quality expectations Identify workflow risks and recommend improvements that improve translation quality and reduce time-to-launch Document repeatable processes that make training and help center localization easier to manage over time Skills You'll Need to Bring Strong understanding of localization workflows, including vendor collaboration, review cycles, glossaries, style guides, QA rubrics, and linguistic QA Experience with Japanese localization QA, ideally for SaaS, technical training, customer education, or partner enablement content Ability to review translated content for quality, clarity, terminology accuracy, cultural nuance, and learner comprehension Familiarity with eLearning or LMS tools; experience with platforms like Skilljar or Parta authoring tools is a plus Comfort working with technical or product-specific terminology that may not translate directly Strong attention to detail, especially in learner-facing content, quizzes, course setup, formatting, and implementation QA Strong project management skills and ability to bring structure into ambiguous areas Why this role matters We want all of our learners should feel like Notion training content was made for them — not simply translated for them. High-quality localization has a direct impact on learner trust, comprehension, launch readiness, and regional enablement outcomes. This role will help Customer Education and Partner Enablement move faster while raising the quality bar: reducing rework, catching issues before launch, improving vendor feedback loops, and creating a clearer, more repeatable operating model for training localization This is a 6-month, part-time role with option to extend. description: Who We Are Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together . We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion. Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work. About The Role Imagine yourself in the 1970s or 80s thinking through how computing should look and feel for people who had never seen one before. That's what we're trying to do at Notion — make software that feels timeless, with the craftsmanship of German cameras, playfulness of Japanese toys, and mass appeal of Coca-Cola. We have no end of fascinating challenges that can only be solved by someone with innate product & UX sense, technical aptitude, great taste, and impeccable craft. This role can be based in either San Francisco or New York City. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. We’re looking for someone who’s excited to work alongside the team during those days. What You'll Achieve: Design product concepts that balance vision, craft, speed, and business potential. Craft every detail of new product features, from idea to UX to pixel-perfect execution. Run projects end to end with engineers to drive your vision to the ship line. Partner closely with our Customer Experience, Sales, and Customer Success teams to understand what each of our diverse user segments need, want, and love about Notion. Use this data and acquired intuition to prioritize, plan, and scope our product roadmap. Work with Marketing to devise new ways to tell great stories throughout the user lifecycle, and across our site, product, help guides and other channels. Create new patterns that are intuitive, practical, and convergent. Evolve our design system intentionally as we scale. Skills You'll Need to Bring: You have well-rounded skills and experience to run projects independently end to end. 5+ years of working experience. You seek to understand the needs of customers then explore and advocate for the strongest user experiences to solve their problems You enjoy untangling vague conceptual problems and have a sharp intuition for the most accessible mental models and flows, so users can immediately start gaining value out of the product. You create clear, intuitive, and visually appealing human interfaces. You care about business needs, implications, and practicality of your designs. You don't get stuck on pretty UI or deep abstractions and can balance between craft, speed, and the bottom line. You have strong beliefs, loosely held. You're a good listener who collaborates well with different stakeholders. You observe and internalize all inputs and feedback to help you reach an optimal decision. You understand how to tell stories using both words and visuals, and strategize the best ways to drive alignment. You value working cross-functionally with project management, engineering, research and data — as well as design peers. Nice to Haves: You've designed and built great tools with small teams in the past. You bring unique strengths and perspectives to the team. We're looking to build a diverse team where our skills and experience can complement each other. You've experienced the pain of fragmented tools and information silos created by them, and have a strong urge to fix it. You're familiar with the work of computing heroes like Douglas Engelbart, Alan Kay, Bret Victor, etc. — and understand why we're big fans. You are a designer who can code! title: Business Systems Analyst
location: San Francisco, CA • New York, NY • United States
description:
Figma is growing our team of passionate creatives and builders on a mission to make design accessible to all. Figma’s platform helps teams bring ideas to life—whether you're brainstorming, creating a prototype, translating designs into code, or iterating with AI. From idea to product, Figma empowers teams to streamline workflows, move faster, and work together in real time from anywhere in the world. If you're excited to shape the future of design and collaboration, join us!

As a member of the Operations & Strategy team within Customer Operations & Support (COS), you'll own and evolve the systems that power our support organization. This role is ideal for a well-rounded systems admin with deep Zendesk expertise and experience with Decagon, who enjoys working across many tools and can jump in wherever the team needs support. You'll help keep our support systems stable, well-designed, and adaptable, while partnering across teams to implement changes that improve both customer and Specialist experience.

This is a full time role that can be held from one of our US hubs or remotely in the United States. 

What you’ll do at Figma:

  • Own and optimize the COS Zendesk environment, including workflows, business rules, automations, routing, permissions, and overall system health
  • Lead improvements to ticket classification, queue design, backlog management, and skills-based routing to help Support scale
  • Administer Decagon and its integration with Zendesk, including handoffs, escalations, and routing of AI-escalated tickets
  • Serve as a hands-on admin across our broader support tooling, including Sprinklr, Gainsight, MaestroQA, Assembled, among others
  • Evaluate and expand agent-facing AI capabilities, including Zendesk Copilot and other agent assist opportunities
  • Own the lifecycle of systems changes, including requirements, design, testing, rollout, communication, and post-launch monitoring
  • Create and maintain documentation across systems, including playbooks, operating procedures, change logs, and architecture diagrams

We'd love to hear from you if you have:

  • 3+ years of experience as a Zendesk administrator or Business Systems Analyst supporting a customer or product support organization
  • Deep hands-on experience with Zendesk workflows, routing, automations, business rules, queue architecture, and channel configuration, plus hands-on experience configuring Decagon and integrating it with Zendesk
  • Experience administering or supporting multiple tools across a support ecosystem, and the ability to learn new systems quickly
  • Experience leading systems changes independently or in partnership with Engineering, IT, Security, or Analytics
  • Strong communication skills, ownership, and sound judgment, with the ability to work effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders while maintaining a high bar for quality, documentation, and execution

While it’s not required, it’s an added plus if you also have:

  • Zendesk Administrator certification
  • Experience configuring skills-based routing, intelligent routing, or classification
  • Experience with Zendesk Copilot, agent assist, or other AI-powered support tooling
  • Admin experience with Sprinklr, Gainsight, MaestroQA, Assembled, or Salesforce
  • Experience with APIs, webhooks, custom Zendesk apps, or scripting, plus SQL or analytics tools to evaluate workflow and tooling performance
At Figma, one of our values is Grow as you go. We believe in hiring smart, curious people who are excited to learn and develop their skills. If you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with the points outlined in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyways. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

title: Copy of Manager I, Engineering - Language Platform
description:
Application Performance Monitoring (APM) is one of Datadog’s premier products that helps developers see inside complex distributed systems. Our SDKs are both the delivery vehicle for APM and the platform on which all of Datadog’s service and app based products (e.g. Application Security Management, Profiling, Data Stream Monitoring…) are delivered. We believe our SDKs are one of our technical moats and are a key competitive advantage for APM and Datadog more broadly. They’re also open-source.

Leading the evolution of our SDKs is a technically demanding and highly collaborative effort. You’ll work with language experts to deliver cutting-edge observability products across our 9 supported languages, with industry leading performance and a world class developer experience. You’ll rethink our SDKs’ architecture, APIs, data models, and protocol to meet Datadog’s current needs and scale, all while building in the open. And you’ll grow your team’s capacity by fostering a culture focused on customer needs, continuous learning, and innovation. 

We’re looking for an experienced Engineering Manager who cares as much about technical excellence as empowering other engineering teams. 

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships that it builds, the creativity it brings to the table, and the collaboration of being together. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our employees can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

What you’ll do

  • Lead, grow, and develop a team of roughly 4-8 library engineers — coaching, giving direct feedback, and empowering senior ICs as technical leaders owning outcomes
  • Own team delivery and productivity: planning, milestones, reviews
  • Collaborate with Product teams to:
    • Reshape and grow our platform capabilities to enable product teams 
    • Define and deliver industry leading, open-source, zero-touch APM instrumentation
  • Stay technically close to the work — apply strong technical judgment, set a high standard for quality, contribute code where it matters most, and keep quality and architecture high
  • Build strong relationships and drive alignment across the language teams and product, backend
  • Shape team identity and culture

Who you are

  • An experienced Engineering Manager with a track record of shipping 
  • A strong and empathetic leader with the ability to build and lead high-performing teams to deliver high quality software
  • An ability pivot from high level product narratives to highly technical implementation details 
  • You have significant programming experience in one or more of: Go, C, Rust
  • Bonus: If you possess experience with one or more of these skills: systems programming experience, observability tooling experience, experience shipping client side software, Go runtime expertise

Datadog values people from all walks of life. We understand not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That's okay. If you’re passionate about technology and want to grow your skills, we encourage you to apply.

title: Administrative Business Partner, GTM - London
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic is seeking a highly organized, detail-oriented, and self-starting Administrative Business Partner to support senior Go-To-Market leaders at Anthropic. This role requires exceptional administrative efficiency and flawless execution to manage leaders' scheduling, logistics, and communications. You will maintain immaculate systems to ensure no details slip through the cracks while providing comprehensive support. As a critical point of contact, you will need to demonstrate exceptional organizational abilities in a fast-paced, high-volume environment, maintaining meticulous systems while handling shifting priorities. Success requires outstanding attention to detail, strong relationship-building skills, and the ability to anticipate needs across teams while ensuring responsive, error-free execution.

Responsibilities:

  • Scheduling and managing calendars for leader(s) and their organization(s), supporting with tracking and execution of action items

  • Building and maintaining organizational systems for tracking and managing inbound requests

  • Managing the leader's inbox and communications with precise attention to detail, maintaining rapid response times and ensuring all messages are swiftly triaged

  • Providing seamless and welcoming experiences for in-person visitors, ensuring prospective external partners feel valued and appreciated

  • Handling travel logistics and coordinating logistics for conferences and events in partnership with comms, sales, and marketing teams. 

  • Coordinating with internal stakeholders to gather necessary information and materials for meetings

  • Managing expense claims and reimbursements for leaders, ensuring timely processing and accurate record-keeping

  • Assisting with ad-hoc projects using your problem-solving skills and proactive mindset to drive positive outcomes

You may be a good fit if you:

  • Are highly organized with the ability to build systems to track and prioritize multiple tasks

  • Maintain a high level of attention to detail in fast-paced and changing environments and take pride in flawless administrative execution

  • Have experience working in heavily external facing Executive support roles

  • Have enthusiasm for supporting leaders in executing their vision, and ensuring they have the necessary resources and information to succeed

  • Have excellent time management skills

  • Have a positive, calm, and welcoming attitude and are able to communicate effectively with internal and external stakeholders at all levels

  • Have a proven track record of handling sensitive and confidential information with discretion

Strong candidates may also have:

  • A strong interest in Anthropic’s mission and deep commitment to AI safety in research and product development

  • Experience supporting executives or busy leaders

  • A security mindset with a thorough understanding of data protection and privacy best practices

Role-Specific Location Policy: 

  • Currently, we expect all staff to be in our office at least 25% of the time. For this role specifically, however, we expect it may be necessary to be in the office more regularly, around 3-4 days a week.

 

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. 

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
£145,000—£145,000 GBP

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

title: Mid-Market Customer Success Manager - Americas
description: About this Role Hi, I’m Denise , and I’m the Head of High-Touch (Mid-Market) Customer Success at Ashby. Our team is passionate about shaping and scaling an exceptional customer experience for our high-touch customer segment, which primarily supports mid-market and growth-stage organizations. I’m excited to be hiring our next CSM as we continue expanding globally. As a member of our Customer Success team, you will help us continue to grow our High-Touch Customer Success function. In this role, you’ll partner closely with customers to drive adoption, deliver strategic guidance, conduct product trainings and partnership reviews, and identify opportunities for expanded use cases and long-term value realization. You’ll also collaborate with a talented group of CSMs across the High-Touch team to continuously evolve how we support companies ranging from high-growth startups to public enterprises. Ashby is designed to be powerful and flexible, allowing customers to tailor the platform to their unique hiring processes and workflows. Because of this, there is a lot to learn. You will become both a product and domain expert, enabling customers to make the most of Ashby and drive hiring excellence across their organizations. Role Requirements: You have a strong track record of Customer Success experience in B2B SaaS (at least two years), supporting customers through the adoption and long-term optimization of complex technologies. You enjoy building trusted partnerships with customers and helping them realize measurable value throughout the customer lifecycle. You have experience managing a portfolio of approximately 60 mid-market customers with over $1.5M in total ARR. You’re comfortable balancing proactive engagement across a broad book of business while building strong relationships with a diverse set of stakeholders to drive adoption, retention, and growth. You have experience partnering cross-functionally with teams such as Sales, Marketing, Product, Support, and Operations to advocate for customer needs and deliver a seamless customer experience. You enjoy becoming a product expert and have demonstrated this in previous Customer Success roles. You create “aha” moments by tailoring trainings, workflow guidance, and strategic recommendations to each customer’s unique goals and challenges. You’ve worked with technically complex products and bring strong curiosity and problem-solving skills to understanding how systems, workflows, and integrations operate in practice You Should Apply If: 📣 You demonstrate mastery of clear communication. You ask questions with precision and can explain complex concepts in simple terms. 🎧 You are a great listener. You see your role as providing the voice of the customer to internal stakeholders so we can ensure that our product roadmap continues delivering value. 📊You enjoy working with a larger book of varied customers, and can effectively prioritise your time to make the biggest impact. 🧩 You’re energized by learning and supporting a complex product. You enjoy diving deep into technical details, navigating advanced configurations, and data workflows, and you enjoy helping customers make sense of them. 🧑‍🏫 You love to teach. Whether it’s a complex report to a very tenured data analyst, or a workflow to a brand new recruiter, who is new to SaaS tools, you see every teaching moment as an opportunity. 🔍 Your peers describe you as detail oriented. You obsess over sending crisp follow-up emails, on time. You take pride in internal operations, like real-time CRM updates. ⚡️ You move fast. You leverage tools/technology to maximize your time. You are at home managing a wide range of customers, and prioritizing effectively. 🗺️ You're energized by an ever-improving work environment. Our team is growing, and continually iterating on processes - we live by our Operating Principle of "Implement Continuous Improvement" 📊 You are always looking for ways to improve your work through data. Why you shouldn’t apply: You thrive with a smaller, more focused book of customers,. Our Mid-Market CSMs typically manage a book of 60+ customers, balancing personalized relationships with efficient, scalable support. You're interested in managing customer accounts with well-defined touchpoints (rather than excited by the fluidity required of early stage CS work) You shine as an exclusively commercial CSM, motivated by variable compensation. While our team's north star metric is revenue retention, we focus on adoption and engagement as our leading indicators. For renewal negotiation and upsell, we have a lovely team of Contract Managers. As such, this role does not currently include variable pay. You’re afraid of rolling up your sleeves. If the idea of getting in the weeds with a customer about the nuance between a time in process report and a time to hire report feels too granular, or project managing a workflow change for offer approvals feels “beneath you”, this job isn’t going to be for you. About Ashby We’re building the next generation of enterprise software, and we’re starting with a suite of products that help talent leaders, recruiters, and hiring managers run their hiring process significantly better. Learn more on our website: https://www.ashbyhq.com/ We are well funded and backed by great investors, including Y Combinator, Elad Gil and Lachy Groom. We have thousands of amazing customers including Snowflake, OpenAI, Shopify, Ramp, Notion, and Zapier (and many others who we cannot name!). Our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers: we have tens of millions in ARR, growing >100% year over year, very low churn, and many years of runway. We’ll share more details once we meet. In short, it's the perfect time to join! 🚀 Interview Process Our interview process is thorough - we aim to ensure each person that joins the team is the right fit for Ashby and will provide ample information for you to assess if Ashby is the right fit for you. The process for this role is as follows: Intro Call with Ashby Recruiting - 30 Minutes Hiring Manager Interview - 45 Minutes Mock Customer Call - 45 Minutes Final Round - 1 hour Rather than a traditional panel interview with a large group, we structure our panel into two focused conversations. This gives you the opportunity to meet with multiple team members in a more conversational setting centered on specific topics, instead of a formal Q&A. You'll discuss how you approach problem solving, dive into a product complexity exercise, then wrap up with a quick closing call with the hiring manager. Benefits You’ll get the time to do things the right way; we put a lot of emphasis on high quality work and avoid quick hacks as much as possible. 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby - do it when you feel financially comfortable. Unlimited PTO with four weeks is recommended per year. Expect “Vacation?” in our one-on-one agenda until you start taking it 😅 Twelve weeks of fully paid family leave in the US . We plan to expand this to employees in other countries as situations arise. Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive! $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval. title: Sr. Support Operations Manager
description: Hello! I'm Allie, Head of Support at Ashby. 👋 Support at Ashby is a strategic differentiator. As we've scaled, we've built out dedicated functions to support it: a Systems Engineer keeping our tooling running, a Workforce Management practice ensuring we have the right coverage at the right times, a Quality program that keeps every interaction excellent, and a Training function that gets new hires up to speed fast. Each of these functions is strong on its own. What we're missing is someone to bring them together. That's why we're hiring our first Senior Support Operations Manager to lead the Support Operations organization: Systems, Workforce Management, Quality, and Training. You'll report directly to me. This role isn't about running any one of these functions day to day. It's about setting the systems, processes, and standards that let them work together, coaching and developing the leaders who own them, and ensuring the systems and processes behind Support match the customer experience we want to deliver. You won't own the hands-on systems administration, forecasting, quality evaluations, or training delivery, but you'll be expected to understand that work well enough to ask sharp questions, spot patterns across functions, and have real problem-solving conversations with the leads who own it day to day. You'll also be a key partner to our Knowledge Management team, helping turn what we know into self-service and in-app experiences that reduce the need for a ticket in the first place. If you love building operational rigor while creating an environment where team members are eager to grow, staying close enough to the work to coach from firsthand understanding, and treating efficiency and quality as two sides of the same coin, this might be the role for you. Our team will be at our company offsite from October 5-9. Applications will remain open during that time, and we’ll begin reviewing them the week of October 12. About the role As the Senior Support Operations Manager, you'll own the strategy, standards, and coordination across Ashby's Support Operations functions. You'll manage through the leaders who own each function's day-to-day execution, but you'll stay close to the work by regularly reviewing QA scores, joining forecasting reviews, and understanding systems changes well enough that your coaching is specific, not just directional. Because this is a new layer of leadership and Support Operations is still being established, you'll have the authority to define how these functions coordinate, where they should be more tightly integrated, and where efficiency gains can free up capacity for higher-impact work. In your first year, you'll establish consistent processes and standards across the four functions, formalize how the functions work together, and help drive measurable improvements in efficiency or quality. What you’ll own: Integrating Systems, WFM, Quality, and Training Manage and coordinate Support Operations' four functions: Systems, Workforce Management, Quality, and Training, ensuring they operate as a cohesive organization supporting our Specialists and Support Engineers. Plan and implement operational policies, standards, and recurring practices that bring consistency across functions while respecting what makes each one distinct. Identify where functions should work more closely together (e.g., how Quality findings inform Training content, or how WFM forecasts should account for Systems changes) and drive that integration. Managing and Developing the Leaders of Each Function Directly manage the leaders and individual contributors across Systems, Workforce Management, Quality, and Training, including several who are new to their roles and still establishing their own operating standards. Coach and develop the leaders of each function as they grow their programs, hire their teams, and establish operating standards, grounding that coaching in specific, detailed feedback. Driving Performance and Efficiency Across Functions Stay close to each function's day-to-day workflows, metrics, and constraints so you can spot patterns and ensure excellence in delivery. Evaluate operational performance and efficiency across all four functions, using data to identify where the organization is succeeding and where opportunity remains. Champion efficiency gains as a core goal alongside quality, not in tension with it. Build the visibility leaders need to understand tradeoffs across systems reliability, coverage, quality, and training investment. Representing Support Operations Cross-Functionally Act as a thought partner to Support Leadership on how strong systems and processes help Support be a strategic differentiator for Ashby. Represent Support Operations in cross-functional conversations with Engineering, Product, and People Ops. Help redefine what an exceptional customer experience looks like as the underlying team and tooling continue to scale. What This Role Requires: Operational Leadership Experience Proven experience leading operational functions in a Support or Customer Experience organization, with depth in one or more disciplines and experience coordinating across multiple disciplines (e.g., systems, workforce management, quality, or training). Experience managing managers or leaders of distinct functions, hiring and developing teams, and building clear ownership across multiple functions. You stay close enough to the work to inspect quality, challenge assumptions, and coach effectively, without needing to be the primary operator for each function. Track record of building or scaling operational standards and processes across a growing organization. Systems Thinking and Cross-Functional Coordination Strong ability to see how distinct functions interact and to design clear ways for them to work together. You use operational data to identify problems, make tradeoffs, and hold teams accountable to measurable outcomes. Comfort working in ambiguity, especially where functions are new and their processes and standards are still being defined. Coaching Leaders and Specialists Skilled at coaching leaders and specialists at different stages of maturity, from those establishing a new function to those refining an existing one. Strong communication and facilitation skills, with the ability to align stakeholders across Systems, WFM, Quality, Training, Knowledge Management, and Support Leadership, tailoring context for different audiences. Genuine investment in developing people, beyond managing outputs. Strategic Thinking and Customer Focus Believes Support is a strategic differentiator, not a cost center, and can articulate why. Passionate about efficiency and quality as complementary goals rather than competing priorities. Excited about self-service and in-app support as levers for a better customer experience, not just cost reduction. You should apply if: You enjoy leading through managers and functional leaders, developing them through specific feedback while staying close enough to the work to coach effectively. You're energized by helping establish an operating model from the ground up, bringing structure, clear ownership, and coordination to distinct disciplines that are still being built. You use data to make tradeoffs, hold teams accountable to outcomes, and prove that efficiency and quality can reinforce each other. You're excited to help build the organization through active hiring and cross-functional partnership, and to shape how customers experience Ashby. You should not apply if: You want to be the primary operator or subject-matter expert in one function rather than lead through managers across several. You need fully mature, fully staffed functions and established processes and standards to step into. You're uncomfortable using data to make tradeoffs, setting standards where none exist, or operating in ambiguity. You see efficiency and quality as inherently in tension rather than as goals to pursue together. About Ashby Ashby builds a suite of products that helps talent leaders, recruiters, and hiring managers run their hiring process significantly better. We raised a $50M Series D in July 2025 and support nearly 5,000 customers, including Shopify, Snowflake, OpenAI, Deliveroo, and Confluent. We’re growing much faster than 100% year over year, with a team of roughly 300 people across 22+ countries. Learn more at ashbyhq.com . About Go To Market We view our Support team as an extension of the product itself, one that ensures an optimal customer experience for customers ranging across all market segments. Here are a few points that should give you an idea of what it is like to work with us: We spend a lot of time building best-in-class products since we believe a highly differentiated product is easier to sell. We also spend a lot of time building a best-in-class customer experience. We aim to offer deep expertise whenever we interact with prospects and customers. We strongly believe that small teams with very talented people and the right work environment deliver much better performance than teams with large headcount. We value a strong sense of ownership, principled thinking over experience, and thoughtful communication (we put a lot of effort into using the right communication channels) - we’ll get into these and other values during the hiring process. You can take a look at our Leadership Principles to get a sense of what we value in People Leaders at Ashby. Interview process Our interview process is thorough and designed to give you enough information to assess whether Ashby is the right fit for you, while helping us evaluate technical reasoning, communication precision, and ownership. Intro call with Recruiting — 30 min Hiring Manager interview — 45 min Take-home assessment — 5 days to complete CS Leadership — 30 min Virtual Onsite — 105 min WFM & Support Ops — 30 min QA & Training — 30 min Support Leaders — 30 min Closing Questions — 15 min Founder interview — 30 min Benefits Benefits vary by country and are shared in more detail during the process. International employees receive statutory benefits and, where available, employer-paid supplemental health coverage. 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby—do it when you feel financially comfortable. Unlimited PTO with four weeks recommended per year. Expect “Vacation?” in our one-on-one agenda until you start taking it 😅 Twelve weeks of fully paid family leave in the US . We plan to expand this to employees in other countries as situations arise. title: AI Outbound Marketing Manager
description: Hi, I’m Tim ! I run Scaled Outbound at Ashby. We’ve spent the last year building the system: campaign architecture, the tooling stack, and the automated email and LinkedIn motion that reaches buyers with thoughtful messaging at a volume no human team can match. Here’s where it breaks. The moment a campaign ships, my attention is already pulled to the next priority. So the work that makes a good campaign great isn’t happening with the level of care it deserves; refreshing and optimizing copy before it fatigues, finding creative new hooks by pulling in from the amazing content library and listening infrastructure, and partnering with other members of the team to create a complete ‘happy prospect > customer journey’. This role exists to close this gap. We’re looking for someone who is deeply curious, with great taste, and who gets energy from optimizing campaigns to perfection, institutionalizing learnings, and scaling the learnings we have from across the business into the most thoughtful, genuinely valuable, and high-converting campaigns. You can think of yourself as the owner of everything that happens after a Scaled Outbound campaign goes live. What you’ll be responsible for in this role Optimizing and scaling outbound campaigns. You will develop highly iterative experimentation methodology sprints to constantly improve the quality of existing campaigns and ensure we land the right message, at the right time, with the right contact. Keep the automated motion from going stale. You’ll co-own the email and LinkedIn sequences with the Program Manager. Sequence refresh, new angles, and killing fatigue before it shows up in the numbers. A big part of success in this role is ensuring automated motion gets better over time instead of aging out. Own copy optimization and conversion. You’re copy-obsessed. You can look at an underperforming sequence, understand why, and then fix it. This includes owning the Twain prompt library that shapes our 1:1 generated copy, tuning it so personalization at volume reads like a sharp human wrote it, not a machine. Turn performance data into action. You’ll own QA and performance analysis for the automated motion and be able to quickly and decisively conclude what is and isn’t working, and then have the curiosity and first principle thinking to know how to redesign and optimize your way into conversion. Collate and integrate materials and learnings from Sales, PMM, and Content. You’ll work directly with Sales Managers, Product Marketing, and Content to pull fresh proof points, launches, and data into active sequences, so the messaging always reflects our sharpest current story. Co-own program-level physical touches. The programs will vary from ICP-tailored gifting (never airpods) to event invitations, and user group meetups. The stack you’ll work in: Clay, Hubspot, Instantly, HeyReach, and Twain. You don’t need to have used all of these before, but you should be the kind of person who gets fluent in a new tool quickly. You’ll Probably Love This Role If You have a creative experimental mindset, strong opinions about what good copy looks like, and no fear of testing unconventional approaches You’re energized by optimization, not just creation. You’d rather make a live campaign convert 20% better than write a brand-new one from scratch You’re copy and customer obsessed, you take time to understand the buyer and can diagnose why a sequence is underperforming, then act on it You read campaign performance data fluently and turn it into the next play You’ve run cold outbound sequences before (email or LinkedIn) You like owning something horizontal that raises the performance of every campaign the team builds The background we’re looking for There are two paths into this role and we’re open to both: Marketing side. Demand gen, growth, or lifecycle/outbound marketing at a B2B SaaS company, where you personally wrote and optimized cold sequences rather than briefing them. Sales side. You've spent multiple years in outbound sales, starting as a BDR/SDR. If you moved into an AE role, you kept running your own outbound. You built your own lists, wrote your own sequences, and sourced a meaningful share of your pipeline from cold outbound at real volume. Either way, what we’re actually looking for is the same: You’ve written cold email and/or LinkedIn sequences and been measured on what they produced You’ve worked in a sequencing or sales engagement tool (Instantly, Smartlead, HeyReach, or similar) and can read performance data without waiting on an analyst/ops You reach for AI to compress your own work, whether that’s research, first drafts, pattern-finding in performance data, or building something small to save yourself time You care about pipeline, not MQLs This role is not for you if You want to primarily write long-form or brand content. You think a live campaign on auto-enroll is done You prefer a locked playbook. A lot of this is defining what “great” looks like from first principles You’re uncomfortable being measured on the performance of a system you didn’t build from the ground up You get overwhelmed by the detailed work of optimizing (sequence refresh, localization, reporting, QA, swapping content) You’d rather own a single campaign end-to-end than raise the floor on all of them Your outbound experience is agency-side or brand-side rather than in-house at a B2B SaaS company You've briefed copy but haven't personally written and shipped cold sequences You need an analyst to tell you what the campaign data says Interview Plan Our interview process is: 30 minutes intro call with Michelle (Recruiter Screen) 45 minutes interview with Tim McCann (Hiring Manager) 30 minutes interview with Harriet (VP Marketing) 30 min take home review Tim, Harriet, Sam Final panel: 30 minutes with Claire (Demand Gen) 30 minutes with Sam (SMB Sales Leader) 30 minutes with Lia (Product Marketing Leader) Benefits Competitive salary and equity. Opportunity to work with a talented and passionate team. 10-year exercise window for stock options . You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable. Unlimited PTO with four weeks recommended per year. Expect “Vacation?” in our one-on-one agenda until you start taking it 😅. Twelve weeks of fully paid family leave in the US. We plan to expand this to employees in other countries as situations arise. Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive! $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval. If you’re in the US, top-notch health insurance for you and your dependents with all premiums covered by us and a 401k match. Ashby’s success hinges on hiring great people and creating an environment where we can be happy, feel challenged, and do our best work. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply. title: Integrations Lead, Partnerships - AMER
description: Hi 👋, I’m Kat :) when I joined Ashby two and a half years ago to lead Partnerships, we had less than a hundred integrations. Today, we have over 300 , thanks to exceptional work from Hannah to take us from 0 to 1, our Product Managers, and our Engineers. As our integration ecosystem continues to grow, we’re looking for someone to take on Integrations as a full scope, including building out our integration ecosystem for new products (like People Workflows). As the Integrations Lead, Partnerships , you’ll report directly to me and be responsible for owning our integration partnerships across inbound, outbound and account management, and being the technical liaison for our Product Managers and Engineering team. This is a highly cross-functional role that requires strong communication and collaboration with Sales, Customer Success, Engineering, Product, and Marketing. You’ll have the opportunity to be on the front lines of trending HR Tech by speaking to inbound partners and guiding them on the best practices for developing their use case against our APIs . Success in this role looks like maintaining a strong sense of ownership over the partner experience and prioritizing how we can be helpful, while being direct and clear about our customer-first mindset. You’ll take over account management for our larger partners, like ADP, and find ways to continue improving how companies integrate with Ashby. What you’ll do Own the inbound integration lifecycle Own inbound integration requests from qualification through launch and ongoing maintenance, using judgment about customer value, product fit, technical feasibility, partner commitment, and Ashby’s priorities. Guide partners through the process—from NDA and sandbox access to API documentation, onboarding, testing, and launch—while choosing the right balance of async and live collaboration. Set clear expectations, keep work moving, and close the loop thoughtfully when an integration is not the right fit or a current priority. Connect partners, Product, and Engineering Serve as the technical and commercial liaison across integration partners and Ashby’s Product, Engineering, Product Operations, Support, Customer Success, Sales, and Marketing teams. Translate partner and customer needs into clear requirements, tradeoffs, and next steps, and help determine the right path: native build, partner-built integration, connector, unified API, or future roadmap opportunity. Help partners navigate API concepts such as authentication, endpoints, webhooks, data mapping, and workflow design, while bringing sound judgment to design-partner and enterprise requests. Own how integration knowledge reaches Sales, CS,and Support, so teams feel well versed on current and upcoming integrations. Own quality, launches, and strategic partnerships Coordinate integration reviews and launch readiness with partners and Product, including workflow validation, feedback, security considerations, configuration, documentation, assets, and Marketplace publication. Maintain the external integration directory and partner-facing resources, and partner with Marketing and Product Marketing on launch communications, enablement, and ongoing updates. Manage larger integration relationships, working with Enterprise Sales, Customer Success, and Product to understand customer needs, enterprise opportunities, design-partner requirements, and roadmap implications. Represent Ashby externally in partner discovery, technical scoping, roadmap conversations, launches, and post-launch feedback loops. Optimize current integrations when updates arise, coordinating scope with Project Managers and aligning with partners and internally. Improve the operational foundations for scale Keep HubSpot and related partnership systems current with partner context, status, ownership, timelines, and customer or prospect demand. Improve swim lanes, handoffs, SLAs, documentation, reporting, and support paths as you operate the program. Automate high-frequency, low-variance work while preserving human judgment for qualification, prioritization, quality review, and strategic relationship management. Work directly with the knowledge base team to build out systems for keeping integration documentation up-to-date. About You We think the ideal person for this role will have experience and skills that look something like this: You’ve worked at the intersection of partnerships, product, technology, and customers—in integration or platform partnerships, technical program management, product management, solutions architecture, implementation, or a similar role. You’re technically fluent enough to understand APIs, authentication, data flows, webhooks, sandboxes, and integration tradeoffs. You don’t need to be an engineer, but you should be comfortable asking precise questions and learning how systems work. You bring strong product and business judgment: you can distinguish between an interesting request, a customer problem, a strategic opportunity, and a commitment Ashby should make. You communicate clearly and write well. You can build trust with partners, set expectations, give direct guidance, and turn messy conversations into crisp requirements, decisions, and documentation. You’re operationally disciplined and improvement-minded. You can own a high-volume workstream, create structure in ambiguity, automate repetitive work, and follow through across teams. You care deeply about the customer experience and can work effectively across Product, Engineering, Support, Customer Success, Sales, Marketing, and external partners. You like building the system, not just running it. You're drawn to finding a problem, scoping it, and proposing a solution, and you don't assume the current way is the right way just because it's what exists. This role probably isn’t right if… You want a role focused only on strategy or relationship development; this role includes hands-on technical, operational, and documentation work. You’re uncomfortable with technical detail, difficult prioritization decisions, or direct conversations about fit and expectations. You prefer an established playbook or a single-function role rather than building structure across teams. You dislike writing, async communication, proactive follow-up, or representing Ashby externally. You are unable to work across time zones or travel occasionally for partner and team moments. You get overwhelmed by your inbox. This role requires timely follow up and holding a high bar for timely communication. You dislike being on calls or you’re uncomfortable leading a meeting that includes customer leads, partner leads, and Ashby Product Managers. Interview Plan Intro Call with Michelle, Ashby Recruiting - 30 Minutes Hiring Manager Interview with Kat - 45 Minutes Panel with Hannah - 30 Minutes Assignment (written) - 2 hours Final Round: Meet the Team - 60 minutes Benefits Competitive salary and equity. 10-year stock option exercise window. No pressure to buy your options until it financially makes sense for you. Unlimited PTO with a strong culture of actually taking time off. 12 weeks of fully paid family leave (US). Generous budget for equipment, software, and office setup. $100/month learning budget, with conferences covered with manager approval. Top-tier health insurance for US employees (100% premium covered). We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply. The through-line in my career has been to build in spaces where no precedent existed. Which is similar to how Harriet is building the broader Marketing function at Ashby: using first principles to think about what we really need to get to our desired results. Over the past ~2 years, our business has grown to be the default operating system for over 5,000 of the most ambitious companies in tech, finance, and healthcare. Our Partnerships team has also grown from just me, to a team of 5 located across the US and Europe. We currently look after a variety of programs that are central to our growth: VC Partnerships, Ashby Experts, Integrations, Community Activation, and more. As a team, we’re focused on delivering outsized value to our partners, customers, and broader TA community – and delivering moments of unreasonable hospitality along the way. You'll be embedded in daily operations (triaging issues, implementing new tooling, and translating business requirements into scalable configurations) while also contributing to longer-term systems strategy as we move up-market and expand our product suite. The person in this role will shape how we build the technical foundation for the next chapter of Ashby's growth. title: Data Analytics Manager
description: About this Role 👋 Hi, I’m Kevin . I manage the Data team and our analytics products at Ashby. I’m hiring our first Data Analytics Manager at an important point in Ashby’s growth, and I hope you have the patience to read a job posting that may be a little unconventional. You will manage Ashby’s three Data Analysts: two core analysts and one analyst focused on Revenue Operations. Our Data Engineer will initially continue to report directly to me, so this role is deliberately more focused on the analytical side of the team while remaining a close partner in the broader data ecosystem. The primary result of your successful management will be a team of analysts with excellent judgment, strong technical methods, clear communication, and a deep sense of ownership. I am looking for someone who can help that team do better work, choose better work, and grow into the next stage of Ashby alongside the company. Rather than begin with a long list of tools or years of experience, I want to share four questions that sit at the center of this role. If you apply, your answer should be “yes” to each. Should we get a chance to talk, what I will really want to understand is the nuance: your unique how, why, and what behind your answers. Can you identify and hire talented people? We will continue to grow the analyst team, and you will play a meaningful role in finding and assessing future teammates. Great analysts combine technical judgment, curiosity, communication, business context, and a willingness to own work end to end. Can you recognize that combination in others? Can you develop and amplify the data practices that let a small team do excellent work? Ashby’s Data team is lean, and our practices will need to evolve as the company becomes more complex. I see this role as an opportunity to improve the ways we prioritize work, review it, share knowledge, maintain quality, and collaborate. Can you lead the team through the transition from broad shared context to meaningful specialization? Today, each analyst can know a great deal about the company and data stack. That will become more challenging as Ashby grows across products, regions, systems, and business functions. We will need to develop stronger domain context and clearer ways of working without turning the team into a set of narrow, disconnected specialists. Can you help the Data team navigate the rapidly evolving implications of AI? AI will affect how our analysts work, how the company self-serves analytical questions, and how other teams use internal business data. Much of that work depends on trusted, well-modeled, appropriately accessible warehouse-derived data. You will help the Data team explore and evaluate the relevant tools, workflows, and partnerships—bringing ambition, practicality, and a high bar for accuracy. These questions add up to a simple reality: Ashby is growing quickly, and the surrounding data needs are becoming more complex. We are becoming a multi-product, global company with more business systems and larger team dynamics. This is a great opportunity at a great company, but it will be hard and consequential work. I am looking for a manager who is excited to help shape the Data function and build an excellent team for its current and future members. Your responsibilities as a Data Analytics Manager To understand the role, it helps to understand how our team works today. Data Analysts at Ashby are full-stack members of the Data team. We do not have a traditional split where Analytics Engineers build models and Data Analysts perform analysis only on prepared datasets. Our analysts work across raw and modeled data, contribute to dbt models and metric definitions, conduct deep analysis, build dashboards and other internal data products, and collaborate directly with partners throughout the company. As a rough sketch, the team receives work through a standardized request process. Anyone can make a request; we triage it, assess the actual need, and decide whether it can be addressed quickly or should become a more deliberate project with a kickoff and plan. We do not currently organize ourselves around universal SLAs, sprints, or points. Instead, we aim to be good partners: communicate clearly, assess capacity honestly, prioritize thoughtfully, and make deliberate choices about what not to do. You will have a lot of leverage in aiding this process well. Ashby’s Operating Principles place principled thinking ahead of reflexively leaning on prior experience or convention. In practice, that means work at Ashby does not always start with “let’s get all the data and metrics.” Data is one useful tool for resolving uncertainty; it is not automatically the first or only tool. That said, as the company matures and more teams optimize their work, demand for data will likely continue to grow. You will help us meet that demand with good judgment. Why You Should or Shouldn’t Apply At Ashby’s current size, this is a player-coach role. You should expect to get hands-on with analytical work as you learn the business and the team, and to remain close enough to the work to guide its quality well. You could be a strong fit if you: Have exceptional analytical judgment. You can calibrate the depth and rigor of an analysis to the decision at hand: knowing when precision matters, when uncertainty is material, and when additional work would not change the outcome. Can produce and evaluate transparent, rigorous analysis. You bring readers along through the problem context, data considered, assumptions, meaningful cleaning or reduction steps, caveats, statistical pitfalls, and practical conclusion. Are a strong visual and written communicator. You care about clear tables and charts, meaningful labels and definitions, coherent narratives, and making complex work understandable without overstating certainty. Have deep hands-on SQL experience, plus working fluency with dbt-style data modeling, cloud data warehouses, and BI tools. You do not need to have owned a warehouse as a Data Engineer, but you should be comfortable working across the analytical data stack. Have led, managed, or functionally acted as a manager for data practitioners in a high-growth company. Formal people-management experience is valuable, but not required if you have demonstrated equivalent judgment, coaching, hiring, and team-leadership abilities. Bring a product-manager-like instinct for finding the core need behind a request, understanding users and business context, and turning ambiguous questions into useful work. Are pragmatic and intellectually flexible. You see data as one important input to good judgment alongside qualitative research, collaboration, user understanding, and clear thinking. Are intimately familiar with the B2B SaaS industry, workflows and organizational structures. Have an eye and instinct for simplicity over complexity in all matters. Have experience in a growth-stage, product-oriented technology company and are energized by helping a lean team scale. You can appreciate the whole distribution as much as a point estimator. Put another way, you shouldn’t apply if: You are looking for a pure-management role removed from the details of analytical work. You will need to be comfortable getting hands-on as you learn the team and helping analysts work through difficult problems. You have only worked in an environment where analysis begins after another team has fully prepared the data. Ashby analysts are expected to work across the stack, from modeling through final analysis and dashboards. Spreadsheet-only analytical work is your preferred mode. Fluency with SQL in a modern data warehouse is essential. You would rather use a metric, dashboard, experiment, or process by default than first ask what degree of evidence is actually needed to make a good decision. You are looking for consumer-scale data infrastructure projects. We have a large and interesting dataset (see our Talent Trends reports!), but we are a B2B SaaS company. Relative to many B2C services, we are small but mighty. You are seeking an in-person work experience. Ashby is remote, although there are employee hotspots around the world and we meet in person at various events throughout the year. You have never formally managed a data team. Naturally, this role is important and represents a combination of different skills. You may not meet every dimension perfectly, and that’s OK. If the dot product of your skill vector with this requirements vector is close to 1, please consider applying, but please note it does not have to be 1.0. Data Culture at Ashby At Ashby, we draw a clear distinction between when to look to data for "the answer" and when to use data to aid principled thinking for decision making. In general, a primary consideration is whether or not data is needed to help clarify points of uncertainty. When data is considered necessary, a secondary consideration is to what depth data will be required. Data questions lend themselves to ongoing "what about..." or "what if..." explorations, which can be important in some situations but are not always necessary. With these dynamics in mind, we do not foster an environment where every decision we make should be backed by data, but we do foster an environment where teammates ask whether or not data will fit the task at hand well. This, in turn, allows us to operate a lean team focused on projects where data provides true leverage to our overall business and product goals. As a related but distinct point, Ashby’s data culture, as far as transparency and access goes, is very open. We share company-wide access to our financial standings, progress, goals, and generally make any data and reporting results broadly available. Outside of constraints related to whether a teammate has access to a particular tool, there are close to no constraints on access the state of the company as told by data or reporting. In general, we would like to continue and extend open access to data throughout the company (with your help!), but with consideration and not as a substitute for principled thinking :) Interview Process Our interview process is thorough, but we aim to be respectful of the total candidate time invested. We aim to ensure each person that joins the team is the right fit for Ashby and will provide ample information for you to determine if Ashby is the right fit for you. The expected process for this role is as follows: Hiring Manager Screen (30 mins) Technical Screen (45 min) Assessment: Mini Analysis and Write-up (45min) Final Round - Virtual Onsite (~2.5, can be split into multiple days) (45 mins) Data Team: Analysis and Productivity (45 mins) Data Team: Analysis and Collaboration (30 mins) Business Partnership (30 mins) Chat with a Founder (15 mins) Follow-Up Conversation + Debrief with the Hiring Manager Note: please do not reach out to the broader Ashby team requesting more information or time to connect. We will diligently review all applications in detail after the public posting period is over. Benefits Competitive salary and equity. 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby - do it when you feel financially comfortable. Unlimited PTO, and we will encourage you to take it. A minimum of 12 weeks of fully paid parental leave, covered by Ashby. For folks outside the US, it may be longer to be in line with regional requirements. Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive! $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval. If you’re in the US, we offer top-tier health insurance for you and your dependents, with 100% of premiums covered by Ashby. In other countries, we provide high-quality supplemental health insurance for you and your dependents, also fully covered by us. Ashby’s success hinges on hiring great people and creating an environment where we can be happy, feel challenged, and do our best work. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply. If you've made it this far and are excited about Ashby, please apply and follow us on LinkedIn to stay up to date!
